---
title: "HDR10 peak"
description: "See the peak brightness Frame Job read from a PQ file, override it when the metadata is wrong or missing, and go back to the file's own value."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

HDR10 video uses the PQ transfer curve, so Frame Job calls it a PQ file. Such a file's metadata names how bright its highlights get, and Frame Job eases them down to white at that brightness, its peak, rather than cutting them off flat. The peak is read when you import the file, and the **HDR10** section lets you see it and change it when the metadata is wrong or missing.

<AtAGlance
  where="Media tab ▸ HDR10"
  tools={['set_media_color', 'get_project']}
/>

## The peak a file names

Import reads the peak by itself, so most files need nothing from you. It takes MaxCLL, the brightest pixel the file says it holds, when that's present and not zero. Otherwise it takes the maximum of the display the file was mastered on.

| The file is | Frame Job looks in |
| --- | --- |
| A video | The description stored with the video track. When that carries no HDR10 metadata at all, the video stream's own (HEVC SEI or AV1 metadata), so files from ffmpeg, HandBrake or x265 are read too. |
| A PNG still | Its `cLLI` and `mDCV` chunks. |
| A HEIF or HEIC still | The `clli` and `mdcv` boxes of its main image. |

A file that names no peak is still read as PQ, and it's treated as 1,000 cd/m².

What the peak does depends on the [project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/):

- **In an SDR project**, highlights roll off smoothly to white at the peak. A peak below 203 cd/m², HDR reference white (the level ordinary white sits at), counts as 203.
- **In an HDR (HLG) project**, the picture keeps display light up to 1,000 cd/m². A peak above that rolls brighter highlights off to fit, and a lower peak doesn't change the picture.

## The HDR10 section

The **HDR10** section of the **Media** tab appears once the project has a PQ file, either a video or a still.

Click the file in the list to see and change its peak. The section's header shows the selected file's peak, for example "4,000 cd/m²", so you can read it with the section closed.

When the selected row isn't a PQ file, the section reads "Select a PQ file in the list" and its controls are disabled.

## Set a peak by hand

Override the file's peak when its metadata is wrong, or when it has none and you know the real figure.

<Steps>

1. On the **Media** tab, click the PQ file in the list.

2. In the **HDR10** section, type a value in **Peak** and press <kbd>↩</kbd>, or click the chevron for a [quick pick](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick).

</Steps>

**Peak** takes whole numbers from 1 to 10,000 cd/m², and its quick picks are 1,000, 2,000, 4,000 and 10,000. A typed number outside the range is held to the nearest end. Entering the value already showing isn't a new choice, so it makes no undo step.

## Use File's

**Use File's** clears your override and goes back to the peak the file's HDR10 metadata names. A file with no metadata goes back to the assumed 1,000 cd/m².

The button is available only while an override is set.

## Where the peak came from

A line under the controls says where the peak came from.

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Mastered at 4,000 cd/m² (MaxCLL, from the file)" | The file's own value. |
| "No HDR10 metadata — 1,000 cd/m² assumed" | The file names no peak. |
| "Set by hand; the file says 1,000 cd/m² (mastering display)" | Your override, with the value it replaces. |
| "Set by hand; the file has no HDR10 metadata" | Your override, on a file with no metadata. |

## Undo and Camera Log

Each change is one undo step, **PQ Peak**.

The peak and the [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) keep each other. Changing the peak keeps the file's Camera Log setting, and changing the Camera Log, even to **None**, keeps the peak.

## Good to know

- The peak belongs to the media file, not to a clip, so two clips of one file can't be read differently.
- Only a PQ file has a peak, so the section's controls are disabled for anything else.
- The peak is read once, at import. Relinking a PQ file doesn't read it again, so set it by hand if the new file differs. A file that wasn't PQ when you imported it can't take a peak after you relink it to one.
- A PQ still takes a peak and nothing else. Camera Log is for video files.
- The peak describes a source file. An [HDR10 export](/hdr/export-hdr/) carries fixed metadata of its own, whatever the peak is.

## With an agent

`set_media_color` sets a PQ file's peak with `peak` in its `color`, a whole number of cd/m². A PQ still takes `peak` alone. `get_project` shows the file's own reading in `media[].color.pq`, where an empty `{}` means the file names no peak.

Two things differ from the app:

- The call replaces the Camera Log and the peak together, so an agent that wants to keep both sends both. In the app each control keeps the other.
- `color: null` clears the Camera Log and a peak override together, and the peak goes back to the file's own reading.

The call fails in two cases where the app can't go wrong:

| The agent sends | What comes back |
| --- | --- |
| A peak outside 1 to 10,000, which the field would hold to the range | "color.peak must be 1–10000 cd/m², not …" |
| A peak on a file that isn't PQ | "media N is not a PQ file; only a PQ file takes a peak" |

See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_color).

## Related

- [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/)
- [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/)
- [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
---
title: "Show SDR Version"
description: "Preview an HDR project as its SDR version, the picture 8-bit formats, JPEG frames and the SDR export get, without changing anything."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An HDR project also has an SDR version: the picture it writes to formats that can't carry HDR. Show SDR Version puts that picture in the preview, so you can check it before you export.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Show SDR Version"
  where="The SDR Version tag at the preview's top left"
  tools="render_frame"
/>

## Show the SDR version

Choose **View ▸ Show SDR Version**. A checkmark shows it's on, and choosing it again turns it off. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's always available.

The preview then shows the picture these outputs get:

- The 8-bit formats: H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, VP9 with Alpha (WebM), Animated GIF and Animated PNG.
- JPEG frames from [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
- The **SDR version** choice on the [formats that carry HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/#which-formats-carry-hdr).

While it's on, the [scopes](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) read the SDR version too.

In an SDR project the picture already is the SDR version, so no pixel changes.

## The tag

A tag reading "SDR Version" sits in the preview's top-left corner while the view is on. It comes after the **Ungraded** and **Selection** tags when those are on. It shows in an SDR project too.

You can still click and drag on the canvas through the tag.

## It belongs to the window

Show SDR Version is a way of looking, not an edit. It reaches the [preview](/timeline/preview/) and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) (**View ▸ Preview Window**, <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd>), and never an export or a saved frame.

It isn't remembered either, so a new window starts with it off.

## What the SDR version is

The SDR version brings the HLG master back to Rec. 709.

- The picture comes back as it was, up to a little below HDR reference white, the level ordinary white sits at.
- A soft roll-off starts there, so a white title stays white, at about 248 of 255.
- Highlights above reference white are rolled off, and reach full white at 1,000 cd/m².

A [gain-map photo](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#gain-map-photos) comes from its HDR picture toned down here, not from the ordinary picture stored in it.

## With an agent

`render_frame` draws any frame as the SDR version when the call passes `sdr_version: true`. The default is `false`. The menu item itself never reaches the tool, so it makes no difference whether it's on. An SDR project's frame comes out identical either way, because it's already its own SDR version. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#sdr_version).

## Related

- [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/)
- [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/)
- [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/)
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)
---
title: "Scopes in an HDR project"
description: "Read the Waveform, Parade, Vectorscope and Histogram in an HDR (HLG) project, where they measure the HLG signal and label brightness in cd/m²."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

In an HDR (HLG) project the scopes measure the HLG signal instead of Rec. 709, and their scales and targets change to match. Use them to see how far a highlight rises above white, and to check that titles and SDR clips sit at reference white.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Scopes" keys="⌃⌘W" tools="render_frame" />

This page covers what's different in an HDR project. For everything else about the panel, see [Scopes](/color/scopes/).

## Scopes read the HLG signal

Turn the panel on with **View ▸ Scopes** (<kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd>). There's nothing to set: the scopes follow the frame they're measuring.

| What the preview shows | What the scopes read |
| --- | --- |
| An HDR (HLG) project's picture | The HLG signal, with the scales on this page |
| The picture with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on | The HLG signal, of the ungraded picture |
| The picture with [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) on | The SDR version, exactly as they would in an SDR project |

## Waveform and Parade

The Waveform and Parade label every line in cd/m². An SDR project labels only 0, 50 and 100 on the same five lines.

| Line | Label (cd/m²) |
| --- | --- |
| 100 % | 1000 |
| 75 % | 203, drawn dashed |
| 50 % | 51 |
| 25 % | 10 |
| 0 % | 0 |

Each figure is the light a grey at that level gives on a nominal 1,000 cd/m² display.

The dashed 75 % line is HDR reference white, and only an HDR (HLG) signal has it. Titles and SDR material sit on it, because they're [lifted to reference white](/hdr/dynamic-range/). HDR highlights rise above it.

The red clip marks stay on the scope's top and bottom edges, so in an HDR project the top one means a signal at the 1000 line.

The Waveform's trace is luma, taken with BT.2020's weights. The Parade shows the red, green and blue signals themselves.

## Vectorscope

The vectorscope measures colour with BT.2020's weights, and its targets are BT.2020's too. That covers the six colour-bar boxes (R, Mg, B, Cy, G and Yl), the ticks on the rim that stand in for them at 2× and 4× zoom, and the skin line. Judge a colour against these targets, not against where it sat in an SDR project.

## Histogram

The Histogram counts the HLG signal's levels, and its luma line uses BT.2020's weights. It has no cd/m² labels.

## Captions

Each scope [slot's caption](/color/scopes/#read-a-slots-caption) names what it's reading, so you can tell at a glance which picture you're measuring.

| Scope | HDR (HLG) signal | SDR project or SDR version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Waveform, Parade | HLG · cd/m² | Rec. 709 · encoded |
| Vectorscope, Histogram | Rec. 2100 HLG | Rec. 709 · encoded |

## With an agent

`render_frame` measures the same four scopes and gives an agent their numbers. In an HDR (HLG) project each scope's JSON adds `signal: "hlg"`, and the sentence that comes back names the HLG signal. The Waveform, Parade and Histogram also add `scale`:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `unit` | `cd/m²` |
| `ticks` | Each line's `percent`, `level` and `nits` |
| `reference_white_percent` | 75 |
| `clip_percent` | 100 |

Luma and the vectorscope use BT.2020's weights and targets, and the vectorscope's `matrix` reads "Rec. 2020". A frame asked for as the SDR version gets an SDR project's scopes, with nothing added. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).

## Related

- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
- [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/)
- [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/)
- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
- [Histogram](/color/histogram/)
---
title: "Blending: encoded or linear light"
description: "Choose how layers mix where they overlap, so a dissolve between saturated clips keeps its brightness and a glow adds light the way light does."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Blending sets how layers mix wherever they overlap: in opacity, dissolves, soft edges, blend modes and glows. Most projects can stay on **Encoded**. Choose **Linear light** when a dissolve between saturated clips dips dark at its midpoint.

<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Blending" tools="set_canvas" />

## The Blending popup

<Steps>

1. Open the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).

2. In the **Canvas** section, choose **Encoded** or **Linear light** from **Blending**.

</Steps>

Blending belongs to the whole project and works in SDR and HDR (HLG) projects alike. Every project starts on **Encoded**. The preview, saved frames and exports all follow the setting.

The change is one undo step, **Blending**. Choosing the item that's already set changes nothing and adds no undo step. The popup still works with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, because it's about the project and not the nest.

## Encoded

Layers blend on their encoded values: the numbers the picture is stored as, which follow a brightness curve and don't measure light directly. Most editors blend this way, and it's the default for every project.

## Linear light

Layers blend as light. Each layer is decoded after its grade, the layers are blended, and the result is encoded once on the way out. You'll see these differences:

- A dissolve between two saturated clips keeps its brightness instead of dipping dark at the midpoint.
- A title fading over video comes out brighter.
- A blurred or feathered edge comes out brighter.
- A glow adds light the way light does.

In an HDR (HLG) project, "linear" means HLG's scene light: the light in the scene, before HLG's curve is applied.

## What it leaves alone

Blending changes no clip and no grade. Layers are graded before they blend, so a grade looks the same either way.

These all read the same values on either setting:

- Grades
- The chroma key
- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
- Luma [mattes](/canvas/matte-tracks/), which cut what they cut before
- The [scopes](/color/scopes/), which still measure the finished, encoded picture

## With an agent

`set_canvas` makes the same choice, with `blending` set to `encoded` or `linear`. It changes the whole project, so it won't run on a call addressed to a nest, where a person can still use the popup. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas).

## Related

- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)
- [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/)
- [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/)
---
title: "Export HDR"
description: "Export an HDR (HLG) project as an HLG master, an HDR10 file or an SDR version, and see which formats can carry each."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An HDR (HLG) project can leave Frame Job as an HLG master, as an HDR10 file, or as an SDR version for everywhere HDR won't play. You choose on the export sheet's **Dynamic Range:** row.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Dynamic Range"
  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
  needs="An HDR (HLG) project."
/>

## Export an HDR file

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>).

2. In **Format:**, choose one of the [six formats that carry HDR](#which-formats-carry-hdr).

3. In **Dynamic Range:**, choose **HDR (HLG)**, **HDR10 (PQ)** or **SDR version**.

4. Finish the rest of the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) as usual.

</Steps>

## The Dynamic Range row

The row sits under **Format:**, and it only appears in an HDR (HLG) project. An SDR project's sheet doesn't have it. To make a project HDR, see [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

The choice lasts while the sheet is open. If you switch to a format that can't carry HDR and back, your choice returns. It isn't remembered for the next export, and an [export preset](/export/presets/) doesn't save it.

### HDR (HLG)

The BT.2100 HLG master, tagged with BT.2020 primaries and matrix and the HLG transfer. It's first on the row and the default.

### HDR10 (PQ)

An HDR10 file: BT.2100 PQ, mastered at 1,000 cd/m², with [fixed metadata](#fixed-hdr10-metadata). It's available on the same six formats as HLG.

### SDR version

The project's SDR version, in Rec. 709. It's the same picture as [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). White titles stay near white, and highlights above reference white are rolled off.

## Which formats carry HDR

Six formats can carry an HDR picture, each at 10 bits or more:

- **HEVC 10-bit (MP4)**
- **AV1 (MP4)**
- **AV1 (WebM)**
- **VP9 (WebM)**
- **ProRes 422 (MOV)**
- **ProRes 4444 (MOV)**

On every other format the **Dynamic Range:** row is disabled and shows **SDR version**. **H.264 (MP4)**, **HEVC (MP4)**, **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**, **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)**, **Animated GIF** and **Animated PNG** always write the SDR version. The audio-only formats have no picture, so the row does nothing there.

### VP9 and HDR

**VP9 (WebM)** writes HLG and HDR10 as 10-bit VP9 Profile 2, and the SDR version as 8-bit Profile 0. VP9 itself can't say which transfer it uses, so the WebM file's colour information is what tells a player it's HLG or PQ.

## Fixed HDR10 metadata

Every HDR10 file carries the same metadata:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mastering display | P3 D65, 0.005–1,000 cd/m² |
| MaxCLL | 1,000 |
| MaxFALL | 0 |

The picture never goes above 1,000 cd/m², so this metadata is always accurate. The [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) in the Media tab describes a source file and doesn't change it.

## HDR frames

**File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) in an HDR (HLG) project writes the HLG picture as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, labelled BT.2100 HLG. A JPEG writes the SDR version, labelled BT.709. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

## Good to know

- There's no Dolby Vision output. None is added to an HLG or HDR10 file.
- [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) changes the preview only. It never reaches an export or a saved frame, so the file is whatever the sheet says.

## With an agent

`export` takes the same three choices as `dynamic_range`: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Where the sheet disables the row, the tool fails with a message instead. Asking for HLG or HDR10 on a format that can't carry it, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, names the six formats that can. Asking for either in an SDR project says to make the project HDR first. Asking for the SDR version in an SDR project changes nothing, and an audio-only format ignores the choice.

`export` returns an id for the job straight away. Once `export_status` reports a video job done in an HDR (HLG) project, its `dynamic_range` names the picture that was written. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) and [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#export).

`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame, and `sdr_version` draws the SDR version in any image format. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).

title: "Precision and bit depth"
description: "How Frame Job keeps the depth of your footage through compositing and grading, which exports carry it, and what stays 8-bit."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job works in 16-bit float, so a gradient from a 10-bit camera file survives grading. There's nothing to turn on. This page says where that depth is kept and where it ends. "Deep" here means more than 8 bits per channel.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />

## 16-bit float compositing

Every video source is decoded to 16-bit float, and every frame is composited at 16-bit float. Blends run there too, so a heavy grade keeps its precision. A 10-bit source keeps its detail all the way to a 10-bit or ProRes export.

A 16-bit float frame takes twice the memory of an 8-bit one, so an export needs about twice the memory for its frames.

## 10-bit exports

The format you choose on the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) decides how much of that depth reaches the file.

| Format | Depth in the file |
| --- | --- |
| **HEVC 10-bit (MP4)** | 10-bit (Main 10) |
| **AV1 (MP4)**, **AV1 (WebM)** | Always 10-bit |
| **ProRes 422 (MOV)**, **ProRes 4444 (MOV)** | Deep: they take the composited frames as they are, at 10 bits in ProRes 422 and 12 in ProRes 4444. See [ProRes](/export/prores/). |
| **VP9 (WebM)** | 8-bit for an SDR picture, 10-bit for HLG and HDR10 |
| **H.264 (MP4)**, **HEVC (MP4)**, **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**, **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** | 8-bit |
| **Animated GIF**, **Animated PNG** | 8-bit |

The sheet's **Bit depth:** row is about sound, not the picture. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/).

## Deep stills

A still deeper than 8 bits per channel, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC, is drawn at 16-bit float. An 8-bit still is drawn at 8 bits. It's automatic and there's no setting: add the file with **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) as usual.

## Saved frames

**File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) writes a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC when the frame shows a deep still or a 10-bit VP9 clip, and always in an HDR (HLG) project. A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip gets the same, when every video track in the timeline is that deep. A JPEG is always 8-bit. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

## Reversed clips

A reversed clip plays from a backwards copy rendered at 10 bits, at the source's exact size and with the source's own colour labels, so an HDR or log clip still reads correctly. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).

## What stays 8-bit

Text, shapes, captions, graphics and screen recordings are 8-bit, and so are thumbnails. In an HDR (HLG) project those layers are still [lifted to HDR reference white](/hdr/dynamic-range/), so they sit with the rest of the picture.

63	description: How Frame Job reads each kind of video and photo you bring in, and what it converts in an SDR project and in an HDR (HLG) project.
64	---
65	
66	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
67	
68	Frame Job reads each source as what it is: ordinary video, HLG video, an HDR10 file, wide-gamut footage or camera log. You don't need to set anything for most footage, because the file's own colour labels say how to read it. The one kind you may have to name yourself is camera log.
69	
70	<AtAGlance
71	  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'View ▸ Show Ungraded']}
72	  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌃⌘U']}
73	  where={['Media tab ▸ Camera Log', 'Media tab ▸ HDR10']}
74	  tools={['import_media', 'set_media_color']}
75	/>
76	
77	## One conversion at the start
78	
79	Each frame of a source is converted once, before anything else happens to it, into the colour the project works in. That's Rec. 709 in an SDR project and Rec. 2100 HLG over BT.2020 in an HDR (HLG) project. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/) for how to choose.
80	
81	The chroma key and every grade then see the converted picture, so they work the same whatever the file was. The file's labels choose the conversion, and a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) set on the file chooses before its labels. The conversion is Frame Job's own, for HLG, PQ and wide-gamut sources alike.
82	
83	An SDR project that holds only Rec. 709 sources isn't converted at all. Its pixels and labels stay exactly as they are, because Frame Job turns the conversion on only when a source needs it.
84	
85	A few terms come up below. A file's **primaries** say which colours its red, green and blue are, and its **transfer curve** says how its numbers turn into brightness. Brightness is measured in cd/m². A highlight that's **rolled off** is eased down to the brightest level the picture can show, rather than cut off flat.
86	
87	| Source | In an SDR project | In an HDR (HLG) project |
88	| --- | --- | --- |
89	| [Rec. 709 or untagged](#rec-709-and-untagged-sources) | Drawn as it is | Lifted to HDR reference white, so it looks the same |
90	| [HLG video](#hlg-video) | Converted to Rec. 709, highlights rolled off smoothly | Kept as HLG, highlights above white intact |
91	| [PQ or HDR10 video](#pq-and-hdr10-video) | Converted to Rec. 709, highlights rolled off at the file's own peak | Real HDR, up to 1,000 cd/m² |
92	| [Wide-gamut SDR](#wide-gamut-sdr) | Converted to Rec. 709 | Converted into BT.2020 and lifted |
93	| [Camera log](#camera-log) | Converted to a normal-looking Rec. 709 picture | Converted to real HDR |
94	| [HLG or PQ still](#hdr-stills) | Converted as a video of the same kind is | Drawn in its own colour, as HDR |
95	| [Gain-map photo](#gain-map-photos) | Its ordinary picture | Its HDR highlights |
96	
97	## Rec. 709 and untagged sources
98	
99	Ordinary Rec. 709 video, video with no colour labels, recordings and stills are drawn as they are in an SDR project.
100	
101	In an HDR (HLG) project they're lifted to HDR reference white, the level ordinary white sits at: 203 cd/m², or 75 % of the HLG signal. They look the same as they do in SDR, and HDR highlights rise above them. Text, captions, shapes, graphics and the background colour are lifted the same way.
102	
103	## HLG video
104	
105	HLG video, such as iPhone HDR video, needs no setting. The file's own colour labels choose the conversion.
106	
107	- **In an SDR project** it's converted to Rec. 709 with its highlights rolled off smoothly. A colour Rec. 709 can't show is eased toward its own brightness instead of being clipped.
108	- **In an HDR (HLG) project** it stays HLG, with its highlights above white intact. An HLG file over BT.2020 is used exactly as it is, and one over P3 or BT.709 primaries is converted into BT.2020.
109	
110	In an SDR project, HLG is converted whatever its primaries. A file whose primaries are absent or unknown is read as BT.2020.
111	
112	## PQ and HDR10 video
113	
114	A PQ file, usually called HDR10, is always converted.
115	
116	- **In an SDR project** its highlights roll off to white at the peak read from the file. Colours outside Rec. 709 are eased toward their brightness, as with HLG. You can override the peak in the Media tab's **HDR10** section. See [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/).
117	- **In an HDR (HLG) project** it becomes real HDR, keeping its brightness up to 1,000 cd/m². If the file's peak is above that, its highlights are rolled off to fit. A peak of 1,000 cd/m² or less doesn't change the picture.
118	
119	A file whose primaries are absent or unknown is read as BT.2020, as with HLG.
120	
121	## Wide-gamut SDR
122	
123	A source with BT.2020 or P3 D65 primaries and an SDR transfer curve, sRGB included, is converted to the project's colours rather than drawn with the wrong ones. This happens by itself, from the file's labels.
124	
125	- **In an SDR project** it's converted to Rec. 709. Colours Rec. 709 can't show are clipped.
126	- **In an HDR (HLG) project** it's converted into BT.2020 and lifted, so those colours survive.
127	
128	An SDR project always works in Rec. 709. To keep a wide-gamut source's colours, use an HDR (HLG) project.
129	
130	## sRGB-transfer files
131	
132	A source labelled with the sRGB transfer curve is read as sRGB rather than as Rec. 709. This is automatic too. Primaries that are absent or unrecognised read as BT.709.
133	
134	An sRGB file with BT.709 primaries never turns the conversion on by itself. It's read as sRGB when something else in the project needs converting, and it looks the same either way. With BT.2020 or P3 D65 primaries it counts as [wide-gamut SDR](#wide-gamut-sdr).
135	
136	## Full-range files
137	
138	A file stores its levels in video range, a narrower band of the available codes, or in full range, all of them. S-Log3 and V-Log files can be stored either way, and the two need reading differently. Frame Job takes the range from the file's full-range flag. If a VP9 video has no flag, it reads the range from the VP9 track's own settings. A file with neither is read as video range.
139	
140	Apple Log, Apple Log 2, C-Log2 and C-Log3 are read the same way whatever the flag says.
141	
142	:::caution
143	A non-ProRes Canon file flagged as video range that actually stores full-range codes looks too contrasty after C-Log2 or C-Log3 conversion.
144	:::
145	
146	## Camera log
147	
148	Log footage looks flat and grey until it's converted, and this is the one kind of source you may have to name. Frame Job recognises Apple Log and Apple Log 2 by themselves. For Sony, Panasonic and Canon footage, choose the curve in the Media tab's **Camera Log** section. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
149	
150	- **In an SDR project** the footage becomes a normal-looking Rec. 709 picture.
151	- **In an HDR (HLG) project** it's converted to HLG instead of Rec. 709, with no highlight roll-off, so it's real HDR.
152	
153	## HDR stills
154	
155	A still labelled HLG or PQ is treated as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, rather than being read as SDR. Bring it in with **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) as you would any picture. This works for PNG and HEIC, which keep their colour space and depth.
156	
157	- **In an SDR project** the still converts as an HLG or PQ video does.
158	- **In an HDR (HLG) project** it's drawn in its own colour, as HDR.
159	
160	Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised, and any other reads as BT.2020.
161	
162	A PQ still has an [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) like a PQ video. It takes a peak but no Camera Log.
163	
164	A still deeper than 8 bits per channel that isn't labelled HDR is an ordinary SDR picture, drawn at full depth. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
165	
166	## Gain-map photos
167	
168	An iPhone HDR photo is a HEIC with a gain map: an ordinary picture plus the information to brighten its highlights. Frame Job reads ISO 21496-1 and Apple HDR gain maps.
169	
170	- **In an HDR (HLG) project** the photo shows its HDR highlights.
171	- **In an SDR project, and in every thumbnail,** it shows its ordinary picture.
172	
173	In the SDR version of an HDR project, the photo is its HDR rendition toned down, not the photo's own SDR image. That covers [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), JPEG frames and SDR-version exports.
174	
175	A chroma key picked on a gain-map photo keys close to, but not exactly, what it keyed before a switch to HDR (HLG). Re-pick the key if an edge changes.
176	
177	## The same everywhere
178	
179	The conversion works the same way in the preview, in every export, and in rendered and saved frames.
180	
181	The timeline's filmstrip and the Media tab's thumbnails follow it too:
182	
183	- Filmstrips of log, PQ and HLG files show the converted picture, not the raw file. In an SDR project that's the picture in the preview. In an HDR (HLG) project they're drawn as an SDR project would draw them.
184	- An HLG or PQ still's thumbnail is drawn the same way. It appears a moment after import, once it's been converted.
185	- Changing a PQ file's peak redraws its strip, as changing a file's Camera Log does.
186	
187	**View ▸ Show Ungraded** (<kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd>) turns off the grades but leaves this conversion on, because the conversion is how the file is read, not part of the grade. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/).
188	
189	## Good to know
190	
191	- Camera Log and the HDR10 peak belong to the file, not to a clip, so two clips of one file can't be read differently.
192	- HDR reference white is fixed at 203 cd/m². There's no setting for it.
193	- A chroma key on HLG footage with P3 or BT.709 primaries, or on PQ highlights above 1,000 cd/m², is close but not exact after a switch to HDR (HLG). [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/) has the detail.

302	## Thumbnails follow
303	
304	Changing a file's Camera Log redraws its thumbnails in the Media tab and its filmstrip on the timeline, so they show the converted picture. In an HDR (HLG) project they show it as an SDR project would draw it.
305	
306	## Before the grade
307	
308	The conversion happens before the chroma key and before every grade step. It comes ahead of every step of the [grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order), Color, Light, Wheels, Curves and Look, so a grade works on the converted picture, not on flat log. **View ▸ Show Ungraded** (<kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd>) keeps it on, because it's how the file is read.
309	
310	If a clip's file has a Camera Log and you also give the clip a LUT as a [look](/color/luts/), the Look section warns: "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." It's only a warning, because a creative LUT on top is fine.
311	
312	## Which files it works on
313	
314	Camera Log is for video files only. It can't go on an audio file, an image or a LUT, and the popup is disabled for those rows. A PQ still takes an [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) but no Camera Log.
315	
316	## With an agent
317	
318	`set_media_color` sets or clears a file's Camera Log. `get_project` reads it back in `media[].color`, with `detected: true` for a file Frame Job set on import. [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_color) has the value for each curve and gamut.
319	
320	An agent differs from the popup in these ways:
321	
322	- Clearing a file's Camera Log from an agent also clears a PQ file's peak override, where **None** keeps it. To keep the override, an agent sends it along with the new setting.
323	- The call fails, with a message saying why, if it pairs a curve with a gamut that curve doesn't take, gives a gamut with no curve, gives a curve and a LUT together, or names a LUT that isn't in the project. The popup never offers those.
324	- An agent can't set `detected` or the file's own peak reading in `pq`. Only import writes them.
325	- The call also fails if it names a nest in its `scope` argument, because Camera Log belongs to the file. With a nest open through `set_scope`, the call still reaches the file, as the popup does.
326

336	title: "Camera log from your own LUT"
337	description: "Convert a log file with a .cube LUT instead of a built-in curve, share that LUT between files, and remove it without surprises."
338	---
339	
340	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
341	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
342	
343	Log footage looks flat until it's converted. When [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) has no built-in curve for your footage, a `.cube` LUT, a file that maps one set of colours to another, can do the conversion instead. You pick the LUT once, and every clip of that file comes out as normal-looking video.
344	
345	<AtAGlance
346	  where={['Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ Use LUT…', 'Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ LUT: name']}
347	  tools={['import_media', 'set_media_color', 'remove_media']}
348	/>
349	
350	## Use LUT…
351	
352	<Steps>
353	
354	1. Open the **Media** tab and click the video file in the list.
355	
356	2. In the **Camera Log** section, choose **Use LUT…** from the **Log** popup.
357	
358	3. Pick the `.cube` file. The panel asks you to "Choose a .cube LUT that converts this file's log footage to Rec. 709."
359	
360	</Steps>
361	
362	The LUT joins the project's media list and becomes this file's conversion, all as one undo step called **Camera Log**. The line under the popup and the section's header then read **LUT: name**.
363	
364	Frame Job takes the LUT's output as Rec. 709, so use a LUT made for that job. Like every Camera Log setting, it belongs to the file: every clip of the file follows it, reversed clips included, and it's applied before the chroma key and every grade.
365	
366	A file takes a curve or a LUT, not both, so choosing one replaces the other. A PQ file keeps its [peak override](/hdr/hdr10-peak/#undo-and-camera-log).
367	
368	If the file you pick is already in the Media list, Frame Job uses that entry and doesn't add a second one.
369	
370	The LUT has to be a 3D `.cube` of size 2 to 65 with the default 0 to 1 domain, and no larger than 32 MiB. Anything else shows an error naming the file and what's wrong with it, and nothing changes. For example: "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/) has the format in full.
371	
372	## A LUT already in the project
373	
374	Every `.cube` LUT in the project is listed in the **Log** popup as **LUT: name**, between the built-in curves and **Use LUT…**. The name is the file's name without `.cube`.
375	
376	To use the same LUT on another file, click that file in the list and choose its row. One LUT can convert any number of files.
377	
378	The popup and the [Look section](/color/looks/) read the same media list. A LUT you imported as a look is offered here, and a LUT you added with **Use LUT…** appears in the Look section's Imported group.
379	
380	To take a LUT off one file, choose **None** or a curve in the **Log** popup. The LUT stays in the Media list.
381	
382	## A LUT in use
383	
384	A LUT that is some file's Camera Log counts as used, even when no clip has it as a look. **Unused only** hides it from the [Media list](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only), and **Remove** asks before it takes the LUT away.
385	
386	## Remove the LUT
387	
388	Right-click the LUT's row on the Media tab and choose **Remove**. The alert says what depends on it, for example:
389	
390	- "It is the Camera Log of 2 files, which lose it."
391	- "It is the look of 1 clip, which keeps its place and loses the look. …and the Camera Log of 2 files, which lose it."
392	
393	**Remove and Clear Looks** removes the LUT as one undo step, **Remove Media**. Those files go back to no conversion, so they show the log picture as recorded. Clips that had it as a look stay where they are and lose the look. A PQ file keeps its peak. **Cancel** changes nothing.
394	
395	The `.cube` file on your disk is never touched. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/).
396	
397	## Camera Log and looks
398	
399	Camera Log is applied before any look, so a look works on the picture the conversion made.
400	
401	If a clip's look is a `.cube` LUT and its file has a Camera Log, the Look section warns: "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice."
402	
403	It's only a warning, and Frame Job changes nothing, because a creative LUT on top of a conversion is fine. If the look really is a camera LUT, keep it in one place: either in the **Log** popup or as the clip's look, not both.
404	
405	The eight built-in looks never show this warning. A `.cube` look on a PQ (HDR10) file does show it, even with **Log** set to **None**.
406	
407	## Good to know
408	
409	- In an HDR (HLG) project, a LUT's output is treated as SDR and [lifted to reference white](/hdr/dynamic-range/#sdr-material-in-an-hdr-project), so the file gains no HDR highlights. A built-in curve does become real HDR there.
410	- If the LUT can't be found or drawn, the footage shows unconverted, as flat log, until you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) the LUT. A LUT relinks like any other file in the Media list.
411	- Relinking the video file keeps its Camera Log.
412	- Camera Log is for video files. With an audio file, an image or a LUT selected, the popup is disabled and the line reads "Select a video in the list".
413	- **View ▸ Show Ungraded** turns looks and grades off and leaves the conversion on, because the conversion is how the file is read.
414	
415	## With an agent
416	
417	An agent takes two steps where a person takes one: `import_media` brings the `.cube` into the project, then [`set_media_color`](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_color) names it as the file's conversion, with `color` set to `{lut: <media id>}`. The call can't set a curve and a LUT together.
418	
419	`remove_media` won't take a LUT that's in use unless the call passes `with_clips: true`, which clears the conversions and looks that name it. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#remove_media).
420

430	title: "A project's dynamic range"
431	description: "Choose whether a project works in SDR or HDR (HLG), and see what the switch does to your footage, titles, grades, keys and qualifiers."
432	---
433	
434	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
435	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
436	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
437	
438	A project works in SDR, ordinary video, or in HDR, which keeps highlights brighter than white. The choice sets the colour every source is converted into, and which exports can carry HDR, so choose HDR (HLG) when you want to deliver an HDR file.
439	
440	<AtAGlance
441	  where={['Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Dynamic Range', 'Document tab ▸ Document ▸ Colour']}
442	  tools={['set_canvas', 'get_project']}
443	/>
444	
445	<Shot
446	  name="11-document-inspector.inspector"
447	  alt="The Document tab. The Document section's Colour row reads SDR — Rec. 709, and the Canvas section has a Dynamic Range popup set to SDR, above a Blending popup set to Encoded."
448	/>
449	
450	## Choose SDR or HDR
451	
452	<Steps>
453	
454	1. Open the **Document** tab.
455	
456	2. In the **Canvas** section, choose from the **Dynamic Range** popup.
457	
458	</Steps>
459	
460	| Item | What the project works in | Default |
461	| --- | --- | --- |
462	| **SDR** | Rec. 709 | Yes |
463	| **HDR (HLG)** | Rec. 2100 HLG over BT.2020 | |
464	
465	Switching is one undo step, **Dynamic Range**, and it changes no clip and no grade value. Choosing the item already showing changes nothing and makes no undo step.
466	
467	The setting belongs to the whole project, so it works the same with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open. A new project starts as SDR.
468	
469	## The Colour row
470	
471	The **Document** section at the top of the tab shows your choice in its **Colour** row. It reads "SDR — Rec. 709" or "HDR — Rec. 2100 HLG".
472	
473	## The HDR working space
474	
475	An HDR (HLG) project composes every frame in HLG-encoded BT.2020, so HDR footage keeps its range all the way through to the file.
476	
477	- An iPhone HDR clip keeps its highlights above white. HLG footage over BT.2020 passes through unchanged.
478	- PQ footage becomes real HDR, up to 1,000 cd/m². Brighter highlights are rolled off to fit, by the file's [peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/).
479	- Footage with a built-in [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) curve becomes real HDR.
480	- Frames are labelled BT.2100 HLG, and the 10-bit exports are tagged HLG.
481	
482	In an SDR project the same HDR sources are converted to Rec. 709 instead, with their highlights rolled off. [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/) has the full table, HDR stills included.
483	
484	## SDR material in an HDR project
485	
486	SDR material is lifted so its white sits at HDR reference white, the level ordinary white sits at in HDR. It looks as it did, and HDR highlights rise above it.
487	
488	That covers BT.709 or untagged video, stills and screen recordings. Wide-gamut SDR footage is converted into BT.2020 and lifted the same way.
489	
490	White is fixed at 203 cd/m² (HLG 75 %). There's no setting for the reference white.
491	
492	## Drawn layers
493	
494	Everything Frame Job draws is drawn as it is in SDR, then lifted to HDR reference white. That means text, captions, burn-in timecode, shapes, SDR stills, graphics, and the background and shadow colours.
495	
496	So a white title sits at reference white, not in the highlights, and a white graphic matches SDR white. Text, captions, shapes and graphics stay 8-bit even though they're lifted. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
497	
498	## Grades across a switch
499	
500	Switching changes no grade value. The numbers stay as you set them, and the grade then runs on the project's working colour, with BT.2020's weights in an HDR (HLG) project.
501	
502	A `.cube` look still reads its values as Rec. 709. In an HDR project the [Look section](/color/looks/) warns: "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709."
503	
504	## The chroma key across a switch
505	
506	A [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/) keeps keying the colour it was picked on. In an HDR (HLG) project it compares the colour an SDR project would show for each pixel, whether the layer is HLG, PQ, camera log or SDR, so it cuts the same pixels after the switch or very nearly.
507	
508	| The key is | Layers |
509	| --- | --- |
510	| Exact | HLG footage over BT.2020, PQ up to 1,000 cd/m², footage with a built-in Camera Log except at its very brightest highlights, and SDR material |
511	| Close, not exact | HLG footage over P3 or BT.709 primaries, PQ highlights above 1,000 cd/m², and a key picked on a gain-map photo |
512	
513	Re-pick the key if an edge changes.
514	
515	The eyedropper works to the same rule. In an HDR project it stores the picked colour as an SDR project shows it, so a key picked there means the same thing in either dynamic range.
516	
517	## Qualifiers across a switch
518	
519	A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) on an adjustment clip doesn't get that treatment. Its ranges are measured on the HLG values in an HDR (HLG) project, so re-pick them after switching. [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) reads an HDR frame at its HLG values.
520	
521	## Exports and saved frames
522	
523	An HDR (HLG) project can export an HLG master, an HDR10 file or an SDR version. [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/) says which formats write which.
524	
525	**File ▸ Save Frame…** writes a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG, and a JPEG writes the SDR version. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
526	
527	To see the SDR version before you export, turn on [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) covers how the scopes read the picture.
528	
529	## Good to know
530	
531	- Wide-gamut SDR projects aren't offered. An SDR project always works in Rec. 709.
532	- There's no Dolby Vision output.
533	- How layers blend is a separate choice, right below this one. See [Blending](/hdr/blending/).
534	
535	## With an agent
536	
537	`set_canvas` switches the dynamic range, with `output` set to `"sdr"` or `"hlg"`. `new_project` has no option for it, so an agent sets it after making the project. A call that passes `scope` is turned down, because the canvas belongs to the whole project. With a nest open through `set_scope`, a call without `scope` lands on the project, as the popup does. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas).
538

60	
61	The sections run down the tab in this order.
62	
63	| Section | What it's for | Shown for |
64	| --- | --- | --- |
65	| **Adjustment** | How strongly an adjustment clip's grade applies. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/). | Adjustment clips only |
66	| **Qualifier** | Narrowing an adjustment clip's grade to one colour or tone range. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). | Adjustment clips only |
67	| **Light** | Exposure, white balance and tone. See [Light](/color/light/). | Every gradable clip |
68	| **Color** | Overall brightness, contrast, saturation and hue. See [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/). | Every gradable clip |
69	| **Wheels** | Pushing the shadows, middle tones and highlights toward a colour. See [Wheels](/color/wheels/). | Every gradable clip |
70	| **Curves** | Shaping tones and hues with points on a curve. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). | Every gradable clip |
71	| **Look** | A built-in look or your own LUT. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). | Every gradable clip |
72	
73	Adjustment and Qualifier show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip.
74	
75	### Which section opens
76	
77	Every section starts closed. If no section is open when the tab appears, it opens the first one you haven't closed yourself. Once you've opened or closed a section, Frame Job remembers that, for every clip and the next time you launch it.
78	
79	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, the sections it animates open by themselves. That doesn't change how you left them.
80	
81	### Read a section header
82	
83	A section's header sums up its state, so you can see what a clip carries without opening anything.
84	
85	| Section | The header reads |
86	| --- | --- |
87	| **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** | "neutral" or "adjusted" |
88	| **Look** | "none", the look and its amount such as "Warm 80%", or "mixed" when the selected clips differ |
89	| **Qualifier** | "off", or what's on, such as "hue · sat · inverted" |
90	| **Adjustment** | The strength, such as "75%" |
91	
92	## Reset a section
93	
94	**Reset** appears in a section's header while the section differs from its default. It returns that section to neutral and touches nothing else, so resetting Light leaves Color alone. On Adjustment it puts **Strength** back to 100 %.
95	
96	To put back one control rather than a whole section, right-click its label or slider and choose **Reset to default**. It's dimmed while the row already holds its default.
97	
98	With an action selected, a section doesn't offer **Reset**. It shows **Clear** instead while the action animates any of that section's rows, and **Clear** takes the section out of the action. On a row, the right-click item reads **Set end value to default**. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
99	
100	## Grade several clips at once
101	
102	Select the clips and use the tab as you would for one. A control changes only its own value on each clip and keeps their other values, so dragging **Exposure** across three clips changes their exposure and nothing else.
103	
104	The value you set is the same on every clip. It isn't an offset from what each clip had.
105	
106	When the selected clips hold different values for a control, its row shows a **mixed** badge.
107	
108	An action belongs to one clip, so with several clips selected every control sets the clips' own values, even if one of them has an action.
109	
110	## Undo in the Color tab
111	
112	| You did this | It's one undo step named |
113	| --- | --- |
114	| Dragged a slider or typed a value | The control: **Undo Exposure**, **Undo Hue**, **Undo Strength** |
115	| Pressed a section's **Reset** | The section: **Undo Light**, **Undo Color**, **Undo Wheels**, **Undo Curves**, **Undo Look**, **Undo Adjustment**, **Undo Qualifier** |
116	| Pressed a section's **Clear** | **Undo Clear** |
117	
118	## The fixed grade order
119	
120	A grade always applies in one order, whatever order you made the changes in:
121	
122	1. **Color**: brightness, contrast, saturation and hue.
123	2. **Light**.
124	3. **Wheels**.
125	4. **Curves**: the tone curves first, then the hue curves.
126	5. **Look**.
127	
128	You can't change this order, so the same settings always give the same picture. The tab lists Light above Color, but Color acts first.
129	
130	A [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) conversion set on the media comes before all of these, and a [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/) follows it, so a key reads the picture before your grade.
131	
132	## Filters around the grade
133	
134	The [filters](/effects/filters/) in the Picture sub-tab act on either side of the grade, which matters when you combine one with a grade.
135	
136	| Filter | Where it acts |
137	| --- | --- |
138	| Pixelate | Before the grade |
139	| Blur, Sharpen | After Color's four controls and before Light |
140	| Sepia, Noir, Vignette, Invert | After the Look, in the order you [stacked them](/effects/filters/#stack-and-reorder-filters) |
141	
142	So a filter such as Noir or Vignette works on the graded colour.
143	
144	[Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) leaves filters on, because they aren't part of the grade.
145	
146	## One grade everywhere
147	
148	The preview, **File ▸ Save Frame…** and every export apply a grade the same way, so what you see while grading is what you get.
149	
150	A clip you haven't graded renders exactly as it would without a grade. A neutral section does nothing to the picture.

168	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
169	
170	A LUT (look-up table) is a table that turns each colour in the picture into another. Use a `.cube` LUT to bring in a grade from another grading tool, a camera maker or a LUT pack. In Frame Job it's a file in your project, like footage. You add it once, then use it as a clip's [look](/color/looks/), or as the conversion for a [log file](/hdr/log-luts/).
171	
172	<AtAGlance
173	  menu={['Clip ▸ Look', 'File ▸ Add Media…']}
174	  keys="⇧⌘I"
175	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Import LUT…', 'Media tab']}
176	  tools={['import_media', 'set_video', 'remove_media']}
177	/>
178	
179	## Import and apply a LUT
180	
181	<Steps>
182	
183	1. Select the clips you want to grade.
184	
185	2. Open the **Look** section of the **Color** sub-tab, and click **Import LUT…** under the gallery. The sub-tab doesn't show if the selection holds a text, shape, graphic or nest clip.
186	
187	3. Choose a `.cube` file.
188	
189	</Steps>
190	
191	<Shot
192	  name="05e-clip-look-lut.inspector"
193	  alt="The Look section with the eight built-in look tiles and None, then an Imported group holding two tiles, Warm Print and Bleach, with Warm Print outlined in blue. The Import LUT… button sits underneath, and the section header reads Warm Print 80%."
194	/>
195	
196	The file joins the project and goes on the selected clips as one undo step, **Import LUT**. If the file is already in the project, Frame Job reuses its entry rather than adding it twice. If Frame Job can't read the file, an error appears and nothing changes.
197	
198	## Add a LUT without applying it
199	
200	Add the file to the project and apply it later:
201	
202	- Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>). A file with the `.cube` extension, in any case, counts as a LUT.
203	- Or drop the file on the **Media** tab. It's the only place in the window that takes a dropped `.cube`.
204	
205	## Apply a LUT already in the project
206	
207	Every LUT in the project is offered in two places, in the order it was added, however the Media tab is sorted:
208	
209	- **The gallery.** Its tile sits in the **Imported** group, in rows of three, and previews the LUT on your frame like any [live thumbnail](/color/looks/#live-thumbnails). The tile's name is the file's name without `.cube`. With no LUTs in the project, the group isn't there.
210	- **The menu.** It's an item in **Clip ▸ Look**, between the eight looks and **None**.
211	
212	Both work as they do for a built-in look, on every selected clip, as one undo step, **Look**.
213	
214	## A LUT is a look
215	
216	A LUT applied to a clip behaves like a built-in look. It comes at the same point in the grade, uses the same [**Amount**](/color/looks/#amount) row, and is removed the same way. A clip that had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with none gets 100%. A clip holds one look, so a LUT replaces a built-in look, and a built-in look replaces a LUT. A LUT also [travels with a paste](/color/copy-a-grade/#luts-travel-with-a-paste) into another project.
217	
218	## LUT rows on the Media tab
219	
220	A LUT appears in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) with a cube icon, and its tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."
221	
222	A LUT never goes on the timeline. You can't drag its row, **Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** are off in its right-click menu, and the same commands in the menu bar stay dimmed while its row is selected.
223	
224	The rest of the row works as it does for footage:
225	
226	- **Reveal in Timeline** selects the timeline clips whose look it is.
227	- **Reveal in Finder** shows the file, and **Relink…** points the entry at a new one. A LUT relinks only to another `.cube` file.
228	- **Unused only** leaves out a LUT that a clip's look or a file's Camera Log uses.
229	- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the file into the project with everything else.
230	
231	## Supported .cube files
232	
233	Frame Job reads 3D LUTs in a text `.cube` file of up to 32 MiB.
234	
235	| In the file | What Frame Job does |
236	| --- | --- |
237	| `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65 | Reads it. The line is required, and it comes before the table. |
238	| `TITLE`, `#` comments, blank lines | Reads past them. |
239	| Windows line endings or a UTF-8 byte order mark | Reads them. |
240	| `DOMAIN_MIN 0 0 0`, `DOMAIN_MAX 1 1 1`, `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0 1` | Accepts them, because they're the defaults. |
241	| Table values outside 0 to 1 | Accepts them, and clamps them to 0 to 1 when drawing. |
242	
243	Frame Job won't take anything else. It shows an error, usually naming the line it stopped at, and the file stays out of the project. That covers:
244	
245	- A file that isn't text, or is over 32 MiB.
246	- A 1D LUT.
247	- A `LUT_3D_SIZE` outside 2 to 65, or a second `LUT_3D_SIZE` line.
248	- A domain or input range that isn't the default.
249	- A keyword Frame Job doesn't know, or any keyword after the table.
250	- A table with too few or too many rows, or a row without three numbers.
251	- A value that isn't a finite number.
252	
253	The message reads, for example, "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
254	
255	## Warnings in the Look section
256	
257	The section warns you in two cases. Neither stops you, and the LUT still applies.
258	
259	| The warning | When it shows | What it means |
260	| --- | --- | --- |
261	| "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and its file has a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) setting, or is a PQ file. | A creative LUT is fine there. A camera LUT would convert the footage a second time. |
262	| "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and the [project is HDR](/hdr/dynamic-range/). | The LUT's values keep their 0-to-1 meaning. Frame Job doesn't adapt them for HDR. |
263	
264	## A changed file
265	
266	Frame Job reads the `.cube` file where it is. If you change the file on disk, the new table is read the next time a frame is drawn. There's nothing to import again.
267	
268	## A missing or broken file
269	
270	If the file goes missing, or can't be read any more, the clip draws without its look. The rest of its grade still applies, and the look stays on the clip. A clip's look comes back once the file is back.
271	
272	A missing LUT shows the **missing** badge in the Media tab, and it's in the list Frame Job offers to [relink](/projects/relink-media/) when the project opens. A file that's there but broken has no badge, and the look doesn't draw until you fix the file or relink it.
273	
274	## Remove a LUT in use
275	
276	A LUT counts as used by every clip whose look it is, on the timeline or in a nest, and by every file whose Camera Log it is.
277	
278	<Steps>
279	
280	1. In the Media tab, right-click the LUT's row and choose **Remove**.
281	
282	2. Read the alert, which counts the clips that would lose the look and the files that would lose their Camera Log. For example, "It is the look of 3 clips, which keep their place and lose the look."
283	
284	3. Choose **Remove and Clear Looks**, or **Cancel**.
285	
286	</Steps>
287	
288	**Remove and Clear Looks** removes the LUT, clears the look from those clips and clears the Camera Log from those files, as one undo step, **Remove Media**. The clips stay where they are. An unused LUT is removed straight away, with no alert.
289	
290	## With an agent
291	
292	An agent adds the file with `import_media`, then applies it with `set_video`, naming the media id `import_media` gave it: `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}`. `media` is required with `lut`, and it's an error with any other kind.
293	
294	An agent can't place a LUT as a clip. `add_clip`, `insert_clip`, `overwrite_clip` and `add_background` give an error that says how to apply it instead. `remove_media` won't remove a LUT in use unless the call sets `with_clips`, which clears those uses as **Remove and Clear Looks** does.
295	
296	An agent can also name a LUT at an action's end. That action stays if the LUT is removed, and draws no look at its end. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#look) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#remove_media).
297

307	title: "Looks"
308	description: "Put one of eight built-in colour treatments on a clip by picking its thumbnail, set how much of it applies, and take it off again."
309	---
310	
311	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
312	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
313	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
314	
315	A look is a finished colour treatment you put on a clip in one click and then dial back to taste. It sits on top of your own grade, so it doesn't move the Light, Color, Wheels or Curves controls, and taking it off leaves them as they were.
316	
317	<AtAGlance
318	  menu="Clip ▸ Look"
319	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look"
320	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
321	/>
322	
323	## Apply a look
324	
325	<Steps>
326	
327	1. Select one or more clips.
328	
329	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/color/color-tab/), and open **Look**, its last section. It starts closed.
330	
331	3. Click a tile.
332	
333	4. Drag [**Amount**](#amount) until the look sits right.
334	
335	</Steps>
336	
337	<Shot
338	  name="05d-clip-look.inspector"
339	  alt="The Look section of the Color sub-tab. A 3 by 3 grid of thumbnail tiles reads None, Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic and Black & White, with Teal & Orange outlined in blue. Below the grid are the Import LUT… button and an Amount slider at 80%. The section header reads Teal & Orange 80%, beside a Reset button."
340	/>
341	
342	The look goes on every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. A clip that already had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with no look gets 100%.
343	
344	## The Look gallery
345	
346	The gallery is a 3 × 3 grid: **None** first, then the eight looks. Each tile is a [thumbnail](#live-thumbnails) of the first selected clip with that look on it, so you choose by eye. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour, and **None** is outlined when no selected clip has a look. When the clips disagree, no tile is outlined.
347	
348	Under the grid comes an **Imported** group, if the project holds any LUTs, and then **Import LUT…**. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
349	
350	## The eight looks
351	
352	Each look is Frame Job's own, built from the same kinds of adjustment as its tone controls. Most also push a tint into the shadows, the highlights or both.
353	
354	| Look | What it does |
355	| --- | --- |
356	| **Warm** | A warmer white balance, a little more vibrance and golden highlights. |
357	| **Cool** | A cooler white balance, a touch more contrast and blue shadows. |
358	| **Teal & Orange** | Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance. |
359	| **Vivid** | More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites. |
360	| **Faded** | Low contrast, muted colour, softer highlights and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture. |
361	| **Vintage** | Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights. |
362	| **Dramatic** | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows. |
363	| **Black & White** | All colour removed, with more contrast, brighter whites and deeper blacks. |
364	
365	## Live thumbnails
366	
367	Each tile shows what clicking it would give you. It's the real frame as an export would draw it, with that tile applied to the selected clips, at the amount they'd keep. A clip at 40% shows you every tile at 40%.
368	
369	The frame is the one at the playhead when the playhead is inside the first selected clip. Otherwise it's that clip's first frame.
370	
371	A refresh starts about 0.3 seconds after the playhead stops or an edit lands. That wait begins again each time the frame changes, so the tiles don't refresh while playback or a scrub moves through the clip. They only render while the Look section is open, so closing the section cancels any render in progress.
372	
373	The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on.
374	
375	## Amount
376	
377	**Amount** sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%. Use the slider, type in the field, or choose 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100% behind the field's chevron.
378	
379	The row only appears when every selected clip has a look. At 0% the look stays on the clip and draws nothing, so you can bring it back later at any amount.
380	
381	Amount is the one Look control that animates. Select an action and the value you set goes to the action's end, so the look fades in or out. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
382	
383	## Remove a look
384	
385	Do any one of these:
386	
387	- Click the **None** tile.
388	- Click **Reset** in the section's header. It's there when a selected clip has a look and no action is selected.
389	- Choose **Clip ▸ Look ▸ None**.
390	
391	The look comes off every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. The rest of the grade stays.
392	
393	## Apply a look from the menu
394	
395	**Clip ▸ Look** does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**.
396	
397	A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some of them carry. **None** is checked when no selected clip has a look. No item has a keyboard shortcut.
398	
399	The menu is available when a selected clip can take a grade. If the selection also holds clips that can't, such as a title, those clips are left alone. The **Color** sub-tab doesn't show for a selection like that, so the menu is the way to reach the gallery's looks.
400	
401	## The Look summary
402	
403	The section's header tells you what's on the selection, even with the section closed.
404	
405	| The header reads | What it means |
406	| --- | --- |
407	| **Warm 80%** | Every selected clip has that look at that amount. A LUT shows its name, such as **Warm Print 80%**. |
408	| **none** | No selected clip has a look. |
409	| **mixed** | The selected clips differ, in their look or in its amount. |
410	
411	## Looks on stills and adjustment clips
412	
413	A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips. The gallery and the menu don't offer one for text, shapes, graphics or nests.
414	
415	On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), the look grades everything behind the clip, for as long as the clip lasts. The clip's **Strength** scales it along with the rest of its grade, and a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) narrows it to the colours the qualifier selects. That's also the way to put a look over a title, or over several clips at once.
416	
417	## Good to know
418	
419	- A clip has one look at a time. Picking another replaces it, whether it's a built-in look or a LUT.
420	- A look comes after Light, Color, the wheels and the curves, so it grades your corrected picture. It comes before the Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert [filters](/effects/filters/).
421	- With an action selected, a tile and **None** still change the clip's own look, not the action. **Reset** is hidden then, and the header shows **Clear** instead when the action animates **Amount**.
422	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) takes the look out of the preview only. Nothing about the clip changes, and an export still has the look.
423	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a clip's look and its amount along with the rest of its picture settings. See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/).
424	
425	## With an agent
426	
427	An agent sets a look by its kind with `set_video`, for example `{look: {kind: "teal_orange", amount: 0.6}}`, and removes it with `{look: null}`. The kinds are `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic` and `black_white`, and `lut` for an [imported LUT](/color/luts/#with-an-agent).
428	
429	`amount` runs from 0 to 1. Left out, a clip keeps the amount it had, or takes 1 if it had no look. An amount on its own needs a clip that already has a look. A misspelt kind or an amount outside 0 to 1 gives an error and changes nothing.
430	
431	An agent can also do something the gallery can't: put a different look at an action's end with `set_action_end`. A change to another look switches at the end of the action instead of blending, its amount included. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#look).
432

443	title: "Copy a grade"
444	description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
445	---
446	
447	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
448	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
449	
450	When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.
451	
452	<AtAGlance
453	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
454	  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
455	  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
456	/>
457	
458	## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes
459	
460	<Steps>
461	
462	1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
463	
464	2. Select the clips that should take the grade.
465	
466	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
467	
468	</Steps>
469	
470	The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.
471	
472	## What comes with the grade
473	
474	There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:
475	
476	- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
477	- filters
478	- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
479	- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them
480	
481	A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.
482	
483	:::caution
484	Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
485	:::
486	
487	The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.
488	
489	## LUTs travel with a paste
490	
491	A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.
492	
493	A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.
494	
495	## A qualifier between clips
496	
497	A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.
498	
499	| Pasting | The qualifier |
500	| --- | --- |
501	| Onto a picture clip | Is dropped |
502	| From a picture clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
503	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
504	
505	## When a paste stops
506	
507	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.
508	
509	Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.
510	
511	To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.
512	
513	## With an agent
514	
515	The menu item always copies each of the picture, sound, text and shape groups both clips have. An agent can list the ones it wants in `paste_attributes`'s `groups`, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["video"]` brings the picture settings and leaves the sound alone. The grade is still part of `video`, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes).
516
