526	title: "Animate a grade"
527	description: "Put a grade inside an action so it changes over time: what ramps, what switches at the end, how each control shows it, and how to take it back out."
528	---
529	
530	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
531	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
532	
533	Most grade settings can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.
534	
535	<AtAGlance
536	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
537	  keys="⌥⌘K"
538	  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
539	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
540	/>
541	
542	## Grade inside an action
543	
544	<Steps>
545	
546	1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.
547	
548	2. Open the **Clip** tab's **Color** sub-tab.
549	
550	3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from where it stands when the action starts.
551	
552	4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.
553	
554	</Steps>
555	
556	Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
557	
558	While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.
559	
560	:::tip
561	An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
562	:::
563	
564	## What ramps smoothly
565	
566	These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's [easing curve](/motion/actions/#easing-curves):
567	
568	- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
569	- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
570	- the look's **Amount**
571	- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
572	- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**
573	
574	## Curves animate
575	
576	Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. An edit to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.
577	
578	| The two curves | How they animate |
579	| --- | --- |
580	| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
581	| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
582	| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |
583	
584	### Animate a curve back to neutral
585	
586	To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:
587	
588	- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
589	- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.
590	
591	The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/).
592	
593	## A look switches instead
594	
595	Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself and not to the action, even with an action selected. A look tile, **None** and **Clip ▸ Look** all change the clip's own look, as one undo step called Look, and the change shows across the whole clip.
596	
597	**Amount** is what animates. To fade a look in, choose the look and set **Amount** to 0 % with no action selected, then select an action and raise **Amount**. The Amount row only shows once the clip has a look, so choose the look first.
598	
599	## Animate a qualifier
600	
601	A qualifier's numbers ramp, but a range itself can't fade in or out.
602	
603	### A qualifier range switches
604	
605	Ticking **Hue**, **Saturation** or **Luma** with an action selected turns that range on at the action's end. It has nothing to ramp from, so it stays off through the action and then appears whole, at the end values you set. **Invert** switches at the end too.
606	
607	If the clip has no qualifier at all when the action starts, the whole qualifier appears at the action's end, and its **Blur** doesn't ramp either.
608	
609	An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on. Unticking a box with an action selected only takes that range back out of the action. To turn a range off, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> and untick it on the clip.
610	
611	### A hue centre takes the short way
612	
613	An animated **Centre** goes the short way round the colour wheel, so 350° to 10° passes through 0° and never visits the greens and blues. Two centres exactly 180° apart have no short way, so the number moves straight from one to the other.
614	
615	## See what the action animates
616	
617	Row marks and the tab badge show what the selected action does to the grade.
618	
619	- **◆** in a row's gutter means the selected action animates that row. See [Read the row marks](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) for all the marks.
620	- **◆N** on the **Color** sub-tab counts how many grade settings the action animates.
621	
622	The badge counts settings, not values. Each of these counts as one, however many values inside it change:
623	
624	- Light and Color, together, for all thirteen sliders
625	- Wheels
626	- Curves
627	- Look
628	- Qualifier
629	- Strength, on an adjustment clip
630	
631	The same grouping decides the marks. All thirteen Light and Color sliders show ◆ as soon as the action changes one of them, and every Qualifier row does as soon as the action changes any part of the qualifier. The Qualifier's range rows and **Invert** read "at end" whenever that happens, even for a range whose numbers are ramping.
632	
633	## Take a setting back out
634	
635	| To | Do this |
636	| --- | --- |
637	| Take a row out of the action | Hover over its ◆ and click the ×, or right-click the row and choose **Remove from action N** |
638	| Take a section out of the action | Choose **Clear** in the section's header |
639	| Make the row animate to its default | Right-click the row and choose **Set end value to default** |
640	| Put a row back to its default on the clip itself, with no action selected | Right-click the row and choose **Reset to default** |
641	
642	**Clear** takes the place of **Reset** in a grade section's header while an action is selected, and shows only when the action animates one of that section's rows.
643	
644	The default items are greyed out while the row already holds its default. Text fields and popups keep their own right-click menus, so right-click a row's label, its slider or its gutter. On **Wheels** and **Curves** the whole section is one row, so these items act on all of it.
645	
646	:::caution
647	Light and Color are one setting inside an action, so **Remove from action N** on any slider takes all thirteen out, and so does **Clear** on either section. To change one slider back, use **Set end value to default**, or type a new end value.
648	:::
649	
650	## How each control shows an action
651	
652	| Control | While the action animates it |
653	| --- | --- |
654	| Slider | The same marks as everywhere else in the inspector. See [See the value change as it plays](/motion/edit-an-action/#see-the-value-change-as-it-plays) |
655	| Wheel disc | A hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead |
656	| Wheel strip | The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, the knob is in the action colour, and a coral tick marks the playhead's value |
657	| Curve plot | The action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour |
658	| Qualifier strip | The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour |
659	
660	The coral marks show only when the playhead is on the clip and the value there differs from the end value. A qualifier's hue band that wraps past 0° gets its knobs in the action colour but no outline. The three wheels are one row, so all three discs and strips count as animated as soon as the action changes any one of them.
661	
662	## With an agent
663	
664	An agent uses `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with the end values in its `video` group: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look.amount`, and on an adjustment clip `qualifier` and `opacity`, which is **Strength**. It changes the clip's own look with `set_video`. It can do one thing the Color tab can't: name a different look in an action's end. A look or LUT that differs between the start and the end switches at the action's end, **Amount** included. **Amount** ramps only while the look stays the same. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).
665	
666	## Related
667	
668	- [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/)
669	- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
670	- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
671	- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)
672	- [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/)
673	- [Looks](/color/looks/)
674	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
675	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
676	---
677	title: "Show Ungraded"
678	description: "Switch the preview to the picture with no grade on it, for a quick before and after, without changing the project."
679	---
680	
681	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
682	
683	Show Ungraded is a before and after switch. It shows the preview as if no clip were graded, so you can check what your grade is doing against the picture you started from.
684	
685	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Show Ungraded" keys="⌃⌘U" tools="render_frame" />
686	
687	## Compare with the ungraded picture
688	
689	Press <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd>, or choose **View ▸ Show Ungraded**. Press it again to go back to the graded picture. The menu item has a checkmark while it's on, and it's always available.
690	
691	While it's on, every clip's **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look** are set to neutral in this window's preview and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). That includes nested clips, clips in a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/), so the grade an adjustment clip puts on everything behind it goes too.
692	
693	The project doesn't change. It isn't an edit, and it makes no undo step.
694	
695	[Scopes](/color/scopes/) read the preview's frame, so they follow the switch and measure the ungraded picture.
696	
697	## The Ungraded tag
698	
699	An **Ungraded** tag shows in the preview's top-left corner while the switch is on, so you can't mistake the plain picture for your grade. See [Preview tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags).
700	
701	## What it leaves on
702	
703	Show Ungraded only takes away the grade. These aren't part of the grade, so they stay on:
704	
705	- A [camera-log conversion](/hdr/camera-log/) on the media. It's how the file is read, so turning it off wouldn't give you the true source.
706	- [Filters](/effects/filters/).
707	- The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/).
708	- Placement, and everything else about a clip, such as its opacity and blend mode.
709	
710	## Grade view tools are never saved
711	
712	Show Ungraded, [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/) only change how this window shows the picture. Each belongs to the window, each is off in a new window, and nothing about them is saved.
713	
714	None of them reaches an export or **Save Frame…**, which always use the graded picture. The thumbnails in the [Look](/color/looks/) gallery ignore Show Ungraded too.
715	
716	## With an agent
717	
718	Pass `ungraded: true` to `render_frame` to draw a frame as if no clip were graded. It's false by default, and the tool's reply says the frame has every grade removed. The tool works the same whether the View menu switch is on or off, and it leaves the switch alone. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#ungraded).
719	
720	## Related
721	
722	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
723	- [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
724	- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
725	- [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/)
726	---
727	title: "Scopes"
728	description: "Open the Scopes panel beside the preview to measure the picture while you grade, with two slots that each show a waveform, parade, vectorscope or histogram."
729	---
730	
731	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
732	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
733	
734	Scopes measure the picture while you grade, so you're not relying on your eyes or your display. The panel sits beside the preview and shows two scopes at once.
735	
736	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Scopes" keys="⌃⌘W" tools="render_frame" />
737	
738	<Shot
739	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
740	  alt="The preview with the Scopes panel on its right. The top slot shows a Waveform with red clip marks and the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %. The bottom slot shows a Vectorscope with its six colour targets and 1×, 2× and 4× zoom cells. Both slots are captioned Rec. 709 · encoded."
741	/>
742	
743	## Open the scopes
744	
745	Press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd>, or choose **View ▸ Scopes**. Do the same again to close the panel. The menu item has a checkmark while it's open, and it's always available.
746	
747	The panel is a fixed column 248 pt wide, the full height of the preview pane, between the picture and the inspector. The picture shrinks to fit what's left, and takes the whole pane back when the panel closes. If the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) is on too, its column sits between the picture and the scopes.
748	
749	The panel is off in every new window. Your scope choices and zooms last while the window is open, even if you close and reopen the panel, and they aren't saved.
750	
751	## Choose a scope for each slot
752	
753	The panel has two slots, one above the other. Each has a popup at its top left that picks one of four scopes. A new window opens on **Waveform** over **Vectorscope**.
754	
755	| Scope | What it shows |
756	| --- | --- |
757	| [Waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/#read-the-waveform) | Brightness across the frame, left to right. |
758	| [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/#read-the-rgb-parade) | Red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side. |
759	| [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) | Hue and saturation, with colour targets and the skin line. |
760	| [Histogram](/color/histogram/) | How many pixels sit at each level, per colour. |
761	
762	You can put the same scope in both slots. Each slot keeps its own vectorscope zoom, so two vectorscopes can show the picture at different zooms.
763	
764	## Read a slot's caption
765	
766	A faint caption at each slot's top right says what the scope is reading.
767	
768	| Project | Waveform and Parade | Vectorscope and Histogram |
769	| --- | --- | --- |
770	| SDR | Rec. 709 · encoded | Rec. 709 · encoded |
771	| HDR (HLG) | HLG · cd/m² | Rec. 2100 HLG |
772	
773	"Encoded" means the scope reads the picture's stored values, not the light they stand for. An HDR project also changes the scales and targets. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
774	
775	## When the pane is short
776	
777	Waveform and Parade want a height of 200 pt, Vectorscope a square of 224 pt and Histogram 140 pt. If the preview pane can't hold both slots at those sizes, they shrink together by the same proportion, and a vectorscope stays square and centred.
778	
779	Below a pane height of 360 pt, only the top slot shows. The bottom slot comes back, with its pick, when there's room again.
780	
781	## What the scopes measure
782	
783	The scopes measure the frames the preview draws. They follow the picture live while it plays, jumping to the newest frame if they fall behind, and update after each edit while it's paused. Until a frame has been measured, a slot is empty and its readouts show "—". The scopes only run while the panel is open, so they cost nothing when it's closed.
784	
785	They read the whole frame, so the project's background counts as part of the picture. A black background beside a smaller clip shows up as shadows at level 0.
786	
787	Because they read the preview's frame, they follow what the preview is showing:
788	
789	- With [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on, they measure the ungraded picture. In an HDR project they keep their HLG reading.
790	- With [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) on, they measure the grey selection picture.
791	- With [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) on in an HDR (HLG) project, they measure the SDR picture exactly as in an SDR project, and switch to the Rec. 709 caption and targets.
792	
793	## With an agent
794	
795	No agent tool drives the panel. Instead, `render_frame` measures any of the four scopes on any frame, counting exactly as the panel does. Pass `waveform`, `parade`, `vectorscope` or `histogram` as true, and `vectorscope_zoom` as 1, 2 or 4 with a vectorscope. The tool's reply gives the figures in words, such as the clipping percentages, and a JSON file next to the image holds the counts. If the measurement can't run, the frame is still written and the tool says the scopes couldn't be measured. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#measure-the-frame).
796	
797	## Related
798	
799	- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
800	- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
801	- [Histogram](/color/histogram/)
802	- [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/)
803	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
804	- [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)

title: "ProRes"
description: "Export a ProRes 422 or ProRes 4444 master for another application, and see what each one keeps."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

ProRes files are masters: their next reader is another application, not a viewer. ProRes 422 is the one to reach for first. ProRes 4444 is larger, and you choose it when you need the alpha channel.

<AtAGlance
  where="Export sheet ▸ Format"
  tools="export"
/>

| | ProRes 422 (MOV) | ProRes 4444 (MOV) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Picture | 10-bit | 12-bit |
| Keeps transparency | No | Yes |
| Odd width or height | Written one pixel smaller | Kept |
| A custom size of a different shape | Letterboxed with black | Won't export |

Both are `.mov` files with these in common:

- The data rate is fixed by the profile, so **Quality:** is greyed out.
- The sound is 16-bit, 48 kHz stereo LPCM. **Bit depth:** is greyed out, because 24-bit is for WAV and AIFF.
- Both can carry HDR. In an HDR project they write HLG unless you change **Dynamic Range:**. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
- [Chapters](/export/chapters/) are written.
- [Fast start](/export/h264-and-hevc/#fast-start) is off, because an editing master has no need of it.

## ProRes 422 (MOV)

Use this as an editing master for another application. It keeps 10 bits of the 16-bit frames Frame Job draws.

ProRes 422 has no alpha channel, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black.

## ProRes 4444 (MOV)

Use this for a title, a lower third or anything else another application will composite over its own footage. It keeps 12 bits and the alpha channel, and the [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`. The colour is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.

It's the only movie format that keeps an odd width or height.

title: Limits
description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.

The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).

## Project size

| A project holds at most | |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | 4,096 |
| Tracks | 64 |
| Markers | 1,024 |
| Media files | 1,024 |
| Levels of nesting | 8 |

Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.

An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.

A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.

Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.

## Canvas and layers

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels in the fields |
| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |

Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.

All nine controls start at 0, and each shows two decimals. The rows run in the order they act on the picture, so working down the list is a natural way to correct a clip.

| Control | Range | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Exposure** | −3 to +3 EV | Brightens or darkens in stops |
| **Temperature** | −1 to +1 | Warmer or cooler |
| **Tint** | −1 to +1 | Toward magenta or green |
| **Highlights** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the brighter half of the tones |
| **Shadows** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the darker half of the tones |
| **Whites** | −1 to +1 | Stretches the tones toward white, with black held |
| **Blacks** | −1 to +1 | Raises or deepens the dark end, with white held |
| **Vibrance** | −1 to +1 | Changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it |

40	It's the only movie format that keeps an odd width or height.
41	
42	A **Custom…** size of a different shape from the canvas won't export, because padding would lose the alpha. After the save panel the export stops with a message naming the canvas's size. Every row in the **Size:** popup has the canvas's shape, and any custom size in the same proportions is fine.
43	
44	## With an agent
45	
46	`export` names these formats `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Both ignore `video_bitrate` and `audio_bitrate`, because the profile sets the rate and the sound is uncompressed. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates).

69	
70	| You want | Choose |

72	| A file every player and upload form takes | [H.264 (MP4)](/export/h264-and-hevc/#h264-mp4), the default |
73	| A smaller file at the same picture | [HEVC (MP4)](/export/h264-and-hevc/#hevc-mp4) |

75	| To keep a 10-bit source's gradients in a delivery file | [HEVC 10-bit (MP4)](/export/h264-and-hevc/#hevc-10-bit-mp4) |

82	## The formats
83	
84	They're listed in the popup's order.
85	
86	| Format | What it's for | File | Sound | Picture depth | Keeps transparency | Can carry HDR |
87	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
88	| H.264 (MP4) | The everyday delivery file | `.mp4` | AAC | 8-bit | No | No |
89	| HEVC (MP4) | A smaller file at the same picture | `.mp4` | AAC | 8-bit | No | No |
90	| HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | A small transparent delivery file | `.mov` | AAC | 8-bit | Yes | No |
91	| HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | Keeps a 10-bit source's gradients | `.mp4` | AAC | 10-bit | No | Yes |
92	| AV1 (MP4) | HEVC's picture or better at the same rate | `.mp4` | AAC | 10-bit | No | Yes |
93	| AV1 (WebM) | The same AV1 picture, for the web | `.webm` | Opus | 10-bit | No | Yes |
94	| VP9 (WebM) | A movie for a web page | `.webm` | Opus | 8-bit, or 10-bit when it carries HDR | No | Yes |
95	| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | A transparent movie for Chrome and Firefox | `.webm` | Opus | 8-bit | Yes | No |
96	| ProRes 422 (MOV) | An editing master for another application | `.mov` | 16-bit LPCM | 10-bit | No | Yes |
97	| ProRes 4444 (MOV) | A master that keeps transparency | `.mov` | 16-bit LPCM | 12-bit | Yes | Yes |
98	| Audio only (M4A) | Compressed sound to send | `.m4a` | AAC | None | No | No |
99	| Audio only (WAV) | Uncompressed sound for another tool | `.wav` | 16-bit or 24-bit LPCM | None | No | No |
100	| Audio only (AIFF) | The same samples as WAV, in an AIFF | `.aiff` | 16-bit or 24-bit LPCM | None | No | No |
101	| Animated GIF | A short silent loop to send | `.gif` | None | 8-bit, 256 colours | No | No |
102	| Animated PNG | A lossless silent loop | `.png` | None | 8-bit | Yes | No |
103	
104	In an HDR project, a video format that can't carry HDR writes the project's SDR version. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/). On a transparent canvas, a movie format that doesn't keep transparency flattens the picture onto black, and a GIF has a rule of its own. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).
105	
106	## Sound in each format
107	
108	Every file with sound is stereo at 48 kHz.
109	
110	| Sound | Formats |
111	| --- | --- |
112	| AAC | H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit, AV1 (MP4) and M4A |
113	| Opus | AV1 (WebM), VP9 (WebM) and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) |
114	| 16-bit LPCM | ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 |
115	| 16-bit or 24-bit LPCM | WAV and AIFF. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). |
116	| None | GIF and APNG |
117	
118	AAC and Opus run at 192 kbps unless a [Quality tier](/export/quality/) says otherwise.
119	
120	A file's sound is as long as the range it exports, including when a clip in it plays faster or slower. A project with no sound exports a movie with no sound track, in a WebM as in any other movie format.
121	
122	## Changing the format
123	
124	Changing the format rebuilds the **Size:** list and returns it to that format's default, because a GIF's default isn't an H.264's. Your frame rate, quality, loudness and range choices stay as they were, whether or not the new format can use them.
125	
126	Picking the format that's already chosen changes nothing, so a custom size you've typed survives it.
127	
128	## Software and hardware encoders
129	
130	AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, by encoders built into Frame Job, so they take longer to export than the HEVC formats, which use the Mac's hardware encoder. The sheet [estimates the time](/export/export-sheet/#estimated-time) for AV1 and VP9, and AV1's [**Speed:** row](/export/encoder-speed/) trades time against file size.
131	
132	## No encoder
133	
134	A Mac with no encoder for a format reports it and leaves no file. The message names the format by its short name, for example: "This Mac cannot export with the “hevc_alpha” preset." Choose another format.
135	
136	## With an agent
137	
138	`export` names a format by its preset, such as `h264` or `vp9_alpha_webm`. [Presets](/mcp/export/#presets) lists all fifteen beside the names in the popup.

148	title: "What an export includes"
149	description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
150	---
151	
152	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
153	
154	Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.
155	
156	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />
157	
158	## The same picture and sound
159	
160	An export draws the picture the same way the preview does, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) you pick, even with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open.
161	
162	View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/), [safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/).
163	
164	The sound goes through a master limiter the preview doesn't have, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). A [track compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) is exact in the file and only approximate in the preview.
165	
166	## Waiting for what it needs
167	
168	Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip, except for a cursor track.
169	
170	| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
171	| --- | --- | --- |
172	| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in Animated GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture set to Foreground) and no file is written |
173	| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
174	| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
175	| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
176	| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
177	| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |
178	
179	Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't finished after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip that will never be measured, because it's silent or under 0.4 seconds, doesn't hold the export up and exports as the preview plays it.
180	
181	While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for masks and cursor tracks.
182	
183	[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.
184	
185	## Missing media
186	
187	A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. So does a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/) whose backwards copy isn't rendered yet.
188	
189	An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence, rather than failing the export. To put the real footage back first, [relink the media](/projects/relink-media/).
190	
191	## Graphics
192	
193	An export draws the [graphics](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/) as they were when you asked for it, even if a graphic's module, the code that draws it, is saved again while it runs. That also keeps a [queued job](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot) stable.
194	
195	If a graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module, the export doesn't start: "The export was not started: the graphic "lower-third" … Fix the module and export again." This counts every graphic in a nest the range reaches, even one outside the part that plays. An audio-only export skips the check.
196	
197	That check is only a compile, so a graphic can still fail part-way through. The export then stops at that frame, names the graphic and leaves no file: "The export was stopped at frame 120 of the graphic "lower-third": … No file was written."
198	
199	## Captions
200	
201	Captions are ordinary text clips, so they're always burned into the picture. They're never a subtitle track a viewer can switch off. To write a separate subtitle file, use [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).
202	
203	## Colour labels
204	
205	An exported file carries colour labels, so players read it correctly. SDR files are labelled BT.709, and [HDR files](/hdr/export-hdr/) BT.2020 with HLG or PQ. A GIF carries no label.

230	
231	## What Frame Job reads
232	
233	| Kind | Files |
234	| --- | --- |
235	| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
236	| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
237	| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
238	| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
239	| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |
240	
241	Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).
242	
243	## Movies
244	
245	Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:
246	
247	| Video | What Frame Job does |
248	| --- | --- |
249	| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
250	| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, using the decoder that comes with macOS. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
251	| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
252	| VP8 | Doesn't import. |
253	
254	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
255	
256	The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).
257	
258	If macOS can't open the file at all and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can [repackage or convert it](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) on import.
259	
260	### Movies with alpha
261	
262	Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.
263	
264	A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
265	
266	### Portrait and rotated movies
267	
268	A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.
269	
270	### Variable and unusual frame rates
271	
272	Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track. A variable-rate file gets a single rate this way too.
273	
274	A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.
275	
276	If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.
277	
278	## WebM and Matroska
279	
280	macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.
281	
282	Add or open one as you would any other movie. A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
283	
284	## Sound
285	
286	M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
287	
288	### Any sample rate
289	
290	Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.
291	
292	### MP3 gapless start
293	
294	Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.
295	
296	This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.
297	
298	## Pictures
299	
300	PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab, or as a background through **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…**.
301	
302	A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.
303	
304	Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.
305	
306	### Deep and HDR stills
307	
308	| The still is | What Frame Job does |
309	| --- | --- |
310	| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
311	| Labelled HLG or PQ | Reads it as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, not as SDR. PNG and HEIC keep their colour space and depth. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
312	| Carrying an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's), as an iPhone HDR photo does | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |
313	
314	A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.
315	
316	## LUTs
317	
318	Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).
319	
320	- 3D only. A 1D LUT won't import.
321	- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
322	- At most 32 MiB.
323	
324	A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…**, a drop on the Media tab or **Import LUT…** in a clip's **Look** section.
325	
326	## Caption files
327	
328	An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).
329	
330	Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.
331	
332	## Which way in
333	
334	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.
335	
336	| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
337	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
338	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
339	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
340	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
341	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
342	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
343	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
344	
345	A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).
346	
347	In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.

361	
362	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
363	
364	Preview Quality draws the preview smaller and scales it back up to fit, so a heavy project plays more smoothly. It never changes an export.
365	
366	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Quality" />
367	
368	## Full, Half, Quarter
369	
370	Choose **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full**, **Half** or **Quarter**. The menu checks the current choice. The preview redraws straight away, paused or playing.
371	
372	| Choice | Draws the preview at | 1920 × 1080 canvas |
373	| --- | --- | --- |
374	| **Full** (default) | The canvas size | 1920 × 1080 |
375	| **Half** | Half the width and height | 960 × 540 |
376	| **Quarter** | A quarter of the width and height | 480 × 270 |
377	
378	The choice is remembered between launches, for every project. There's no keyboard shortcut, and no agent tool sets it. The [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture, so it draws at the same quality.
379	
380	## What it changes
381	
382	Quality only affects the preview. It never changes an export, a [saved frame](/export/save-frame/) or a frame an agent renders.
383	
384	A lower choice saves the work of drawing each pixel of the picture. Decoding your footage, drawing shadows and playing the sound cost the same at every choice, so a project held back by those won't speed up as much.
385	
386	## Good to know
387	
388	The picture always keeps the canvas's exact shape, so that handles stay in the right place on it. On an awkward canvas size that means the preview can draw a little larger than the fraction, never smaller:
389	
390	| Canvas | Half | Quarter |
391	| --- | --- | --- |
392	| 999 × 666 | 501 × 334 | 252 × 168 |
393	| 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 |
394	
395	A canvas whose sides share no common factor, like 1001 × 667, can't be scaled down evenly, so it draws at full size at every choice.

418	## What it shows
419	
420	The picture keeps the canvas's shape, letterboxed to fit the pane to the left of the inspector. Under it, a small caption gives the canvas size and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`.
421	
422	The preview is also where you work on the picture: selecting clips, then moving, scaling, rotating and cropping them. That's covered in [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/), and zooming it in [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).
423	
424	Two settings change how the preview is drawn, and neither touches an export:
425	
426	- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) draws it smaller, so heavy projects play more smoothly.
427	- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture in a second window, for another display.
428	
429	## Preview tags
430	
431	Small tags in the top-left corner of the pane tell you when the picture isn't the plain one. Each shows only while its **View** item is on.
432	
433	| Tag | Means | View item |
434	| --- | --- | --- |
435	| **Ungraded** | The picture shows no clip's grade. | [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) |
436	| **Selection** | The picture shows which pixels the selected adjustment clip's qualifier picks. | [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) |
437	| **SDR Version** | The picture shows the project's SDR version. | [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) |
438	
439	<Shot
440	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
441	  alt="The preview pane with the Ungraded tag in its top-left corner, the picture with its caption 960 × 540 · 30 fps underneath, and the scopes panel beside it showing a waveform over a vectorscope."
442	/>
443	
444	The tags sit in that order, and a hidden tag leaves no space, so **Selection** moves into the corner when **Ungraded** is off. **SDR Version** shows in an SDR project too, where the picture doesn't change.
445	
446	## Other View items
447	
448	The **View** menu holds the other switches for the preview. Each has its own page.
449	
450	| Item | Keys | What it does | Remembered |
451	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
452	| [**Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/) | | Shows the title-safe and action-safe guides, the same as the toolbar's **Safe** box. Checked when on. | Yes |
453	| [**Show Ungraded**](/color/show-ungraded/) | <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd> | Shows the picture as if no clip were graded. | No |
454	| [**Show Selection**](/color/show-selection/) | | Shows what an adjustment clip's qualifier picks. It needs a selected adjustment clip to turn on. | No |
455	| [**Show SDR Version**](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) | | Shows an HDR project's SDR version. | No |
456	| [**Show Subjects**](/framing/show-subjects/) | | Draws the faces, people and salient regions found for the selected clip. | No |
457	| [**Scopes**](/color/scopes/) | <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> | Shows the scopes panel beside the picture. | No |
458	| [**Loudness Meter**](/audio/loudness-meter/) | <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd> | Shows the live loudness column beside the picture. | No |
459	
460	Remembered means between launches, for every project. The items that aren't remembered start off in each new window, as the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) does, and none of these changes an export.
461	
462	**View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) sits nearby but doesn't change the picture. It opens the inspector's Assistant tab, beside the preview. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).

476	
477	Play the timeline to watch your edit. It all runs from the keyboard: <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> shuttle forwards or backwards at up to four times speed, and the arrow keys step to the frame you want.
478	
479	<AtAGlance
480	  keys={['Space', 'J', 'K', 'L', '←', '→', '⇧←', '⇧→']}
481	  where="The Play and Pause button in the toolbar"
482	  tools="set_playhead"
483	/>
484	
485	## Play and pause
486	
487	Press <kbd>Space</kbd>, or the Play button among the toolbar's transport buttons. The button shows Play or Pause to match, and it stays in the same spot. There's no menu item for it.
488	
489	<kbd>Space</kbd> works from wherever the focus is in the window, with a few exceptions:
490	
491	| Where you are | What <kbd>Space</kbd> does |
492	| --- | --- |
493	| Typing in a text field, the Text tab's text area, the canvas text editor or the Media tab's search field | Types a space. Typing ends with <kbd>Return</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click outside the field, and <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight after. |
494	| On the preview canvas | Plays or pauses when you let go, because the press gets ready to [pan](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). If you panned while holding it, letting go does nothing. |
495	| On a button, pop-up or segmented control focused with Full Keyboard Access | Presses that control. |
496	| With a sheet open | Doesn't play or pause. |
497	
498	<kbd>⇧Space</kbd> plays and pauses too. Any other modifier leaves the key alone. Holding <kbd>Space</kbd> down doesn't toggle playback over and over.
499	
500	## J, K and L
501	
502	<kbd>L</kbd> plays forward, <kbd>J</kbd> plays in reverse and <kbd>K</kbd> pauses.
503	
504	| Press | What happens |
505	| --- | --- |
506	| <kbd>L</kbd> or <kbd>J</kbd> while stopped | Plays at ×1 in that direction. |
507	| The same key again | Steps up from ×1 to ×2 to ×4. At ×4 it stays at ×4. |
508	| The opposite key | Goes straight to ×1 in that direction. |
509	| <kbd>K</kbd> | Pauses. |
510	
511	These keys also work from the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). They don't work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open.
512	
513	## Step frames
514	
515	<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> pause playback and move the playhead one frame. With <kbd>⇧</kbd>, they move ten. This is the way to place a cut exactly.
516	
517	Stepping is silent, unlike a [scrub on the ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/#scrub-on-the-ruler). In the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/), these keys move by word instead.
518	
519	To go further in one press, see [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
520	
521	## At the end
522	
523	Playback stops at the end of the timeline, and the playhead stays there. Press <kbd>Home</kbd> to [go back to the start](/timeline/move-the-playhead/). With [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, playback goes back to the start of the loop instead.
524	
525	An empty timeline has nothing to play, so Play, <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> beep.
526	
527	## After an edit
528	
529	You can edit while the timeline plays. What you notice depends on what you changed.
530	
531	### Look-only edits
532	
533	A change that only alters how something looks, such as a clip's position, a colour or some text, redraws the frame in place. Playback isn't interrupted.
534	
535	### Structural edits
536	
537	A move, a trim, a new clip or anything else that changes the timeline's shape makes Frame Job rebuild what the preview plays, in the background. So does a change to the sound, such as volume, pan or the compressor. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the same speed. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
538	
539	### Failed rebuild
540	
541	If a rebuild fails, Frame Job shows the error and the previous version of the timeline keeps playing.

574	## Add media
575	
576	<Steps>
577	
578	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>), or **Add Media…** at the top of the Media tab.
579	
580	2. Pick one or more files, and choose **Open**.
581	
582	</Steps>
583	
584	Frame Job checks every file, then adds the ones it can read to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) together, as one undo step. The step is called **Add Media**, or **Add 3 Media Files** for three.
585	
586	The files are in the Media tab, not on the timeline. [Place them](/editing/add-clips/) from there. Thumbnails and waveforms are built in the background, so they fill in a moment later.
587	
588	Adding a file that's already in the list changes nothing. A file Frame Job can't read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added.
589	
590	## Drop on the Media tab
591	
592	Drag files from the Finder onto the Media tab to add them to this project. It works like **Add Media…**, with one difference: a drop has no list of allowed types, so Frame Job tries every file you drop. That's how a format the panels don't list gets in.
593	
594	A Finder drop anywhere else on the window, such as the canvas or the timeline, doesn't add to this project. It opens the file as a new project of its own, as a drop on the Dock icon does. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
595	
596	## What each way takes
597	
598	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels only let you pick the types they list. To bring in anything else, drop it on the Media tab.
599	
600	| Files | **Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…**, or a drop on the window or the Dock | A drop on the Media tab |
601	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
602	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
603	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
604	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
605	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
606	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
607	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
608	
609	A `.cube` is imported, never opened. It sits in the Media tab and you apply it to clips as a [look](/color/luts/), or to a file as its [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/). It never goes on the timeline.
610	
611	Caption files aren't media. Bring an `.srt` in with [Import Captions](/captions/import-captions/). Every format and codec Frame Job reads is listed in [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
612	
613	## Referenced, not copied
614	
615	A project remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small, but it depends on your footage staying put. If you move a file, the bookmark often finds it again.
616	
617	When you want a package that holds everything it needs, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
618	
619	WebM and Matroska files, and anything converted with ffmpeg, are the exception: Frame Job reads those from a copy it keeps in its own folder. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
620	
621	## A project always opens
622	
623	A project opens even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, and their rows in the Media tab wear the **missing** badge.
624	
625	Those clips still export, showing the slate and with no sound. To bring them back, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
626	
627	## Codecs this Mac can't decode
628	
629	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame. If nothing on this Mac can decode it, the file is left out and an alert names the codec.
630	
631	| The alert says | What it means |
632	| --- | --- |
633	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | VP8 doesn't import. |
634	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | AV1 needs a hardware decoder, which this Mac doesn't have. |
635	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | VP9 Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. Profiles 0 and 2 do. |
636	
637	Any other codec gets the same sentence with its four-character code in place of a name. There's no way past these, and [ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) isn't offered.
638	
639	A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports when some of its data is damaged.
640	
641	## Import errors
642	
643	| The alert says | What it means |
644	| --- | --- |
645	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
646	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
647	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took more than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume. |
648	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The `.cube` can't be read. The alert names the line and the problem. |
649	
650	If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job may offer to convert a file before it shows the first two of these. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
651	
652	## Good to know
653	
654	- A project holds at most 1,024 media files.
655	- Undoing an import takes the files out of the project and leaves them on disk.
656	
657	## With an agent
658	
659	[`import_media`](/mcp/tools-media/#import_media) does what **Add Media…** does, one file at a time, and it never stops to ask a question. It takes the file's path, absolute or starting with `~`, and gives back the new media id with what it found in the file: its kind, length, size, frame rate, and whether it has video, sound or transparency. Place the file with [`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_clip).
660	
661	[`add_media`](/mcp/tools-media/#add_media) is different: it adds an entry from a description you supply and doesn't look at the file. Only the path is needed, and a path already in the list changes nothing. Use it only to replay a project's own JSON. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

196	title: Troubleshooting
197	description: Find out why a command is greyed, an edit is refused, a file won't open, a clip is silent or an export stops, and what to do next.
198	---
199	
200	Frame Job says why it won't do something, in a sentence or a tooltip. This page starts from what you see and tells you what it means and what to do. For the numbers behind these answers, see [Limits](/reference/limits/).
201	
202	## A command is greyed out
203	
204	Every menu item has a rule for when it's on. [Menus](/reference/menus/) and [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/) give each item's rule. A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed.
205	
206	If the item should be on, check these first:
207	
208	| Check | Why it matters |
209	| --- | --- |
210	| The selection | Many commands need a clip selected, or a certain kind of clip. |
211	| A sheet | While a sheet is open, every editor command is off. Close the sheet first. |
212	| A nest | With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these are off: **New Project from Range…**, **Make Vertical Version…**, **Rename Graphic…**, **Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker**, **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** and **Text Behind Subject**. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. |
213	| A text field | **Open Nest**, **Close Nest**, **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** are off while you type, because their keys edit the text. |
214	| A key | A command that needs your own key stays in the menu, greyed, and its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)". Rest the pointer on it to see which key and where to set it. Saving the key turns it on at once. See [A feature asks for a key](#a-feature-asks-for-a-key). |
215	
216	## A key does nothing
217	
218	Single-letter keys and the arrow keys belong to the editor window, and they stand down in two cases.
219	
220	- **You're typing in a field.** Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click outside the field, to give the keys back to the editor.
221	- **A sheet is open.** Close it first. In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the main button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> cancels.
222	
223	One more thing can catch you out: with a point selected on a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the clip.
224	
225	See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/) and [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).
226	
227	## An edit is refused
228	
229	When the project's rules won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the rule's own sentence appears at the foot of the inspector after "Refused: ":
230	
231	> Refused: clips 4 and 7 would overlap by 120000 ticks, more than half of the shorter clip (100000 ticks)
232	
233	The sentence stays until the project changes or you click it. It's exact rather than friendly. The clip numbers are Frame Job's own, not positions on the timeline, and a [tick](/reference/glossary/#projects-and-the-timeline) is 1/600,000 of a second. So this one says the overlap would be 0.2 s, and half of the shorter clip is 0.17 s.
234	
235	The rules you'll meet most:
236	
237	| Rule | What it means |
238	| --- | --- |
239	| The overlap rule | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. |
240	| A locked track | Its clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and you can't insert onto it or close a gap on it. Unlock it with its [lock button](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
241	| The one-frame minimum | Trims and rolls leave a clip at least one frame long. |
242	| The ends of the file | A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. |
243	
244	Two other results look similar:
245	
246	- **A beep with no message** means the edit would have changed nothing, such as a slip already at the end of the footage. No rule was broken.
247	- **An error alert** means Frame Job couldn't use the request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range.
248	
249	During a drag, positions the rules won't allow are skipped, and the clip waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts.
250	
251	See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
252	
253	## A project won't open
254	
255	A project that can't be read fails with a message naming the problem, and Frame Job doesn't rewrite the package.
256	
257	| Message | What to do |
258	| --- | --- |
259	| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The project file inside the package is damaged. Open a backup copy if you have one. |
260	| "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it" | A newer Frame Job saved it. [Update Frame Job](/getting-started/updates/). |
261	| "too many clips: 5000 (max 4096)", or the same for tracks, markers or media | The file is past one of the [project limits](/reference/limits/#project-size). |
262	
263	Files that have moved don't stop a project opening, and neither does a damaged `cache/` folder. For moved files, see [Clips show a slate](#clips-show-a-slate). Also see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
264	
265	## A file won't import
266	
267	Frame Job tells you which file it couldn't add and why.
268	
269	| Message | What it means |
270	| --- | --- |
271	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | This Mac has no AV1 decoder. |
272	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | Only those two VP9 profiles import. |
273	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | This Mac has no decoder for that codec. Other codecs it can't decode get the same sentence with their own name. |
274	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
275	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
276	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because of a stalled network volume. |
277	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The message names the line of the file and what's wrong with it. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). |
278	| "Not enough free space to open *file*…" | A WebM or Matroska file needs room for its copy. The sentence says how much. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). |
279	
280	A file in a codec this Mac decodes still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
281	
282	If macOS can't open a file, you can repackage or convert it with your own ffmpeg. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
283	
284	If the **File ▸ Add Media…** panel won't let you choose a file, drop it on the Media tab instead. The panel lists only the common types. See [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
285	
286	An agent's `import_media` reports these reasons too.
287	
288	## Clips show a slate
289	
290	A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place and show a slate, and their rows in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wear the **missing** badge.
291	
292	When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once. Choose **Locate…** for a file, then **Relink**. Frame Job also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, so a shoot moved as one folder is usually found in one go. To relink a file later, use **Relink…** on its row in the Media tab. An agent uses `relink_media`.
293	
294	Two other cases show a slate or leave media missing:
295	
296	- A reversed clip shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
297	- A [conversion made with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#a-lost-conversion-stays-missing) that's gone from Frame Job's [Rewrapped folder](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder) stays missing until you relink it. A WebM or MKV copy that's gone is [made again](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#if-a-copy-goes-missing) when the project opens, as long as the original is still there.
298	
299	See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
300	
301	## A clip is silent
302	
303	Check these in order. A muted clip, a muted track and a track silenced by a solo all draw the waveform faded.
304	
305	| Check | What to do |
306	| --- | --- |
307	| The clip's own sound | The clip may be muted in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/), or its [sound turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). |
308	| The track's **Mute** | A muted track is silent. Mute wins over Solo, so a track that's muted and soloed stays silent. |
309	| **Solo** on another track | While any track is soloed, the others are silent, even if the soloed track has nothing on it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
310	| The clip's rate | Above ×12 a clip has no sound, and the Speed section says "Audio is silent above ×12". On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/). |
311	| Whether its sound has rendered | A ramp's sound, and a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, is silent in the preview until its render finishes. A failed render stays failed until the clip's timing changes or you reopen Frame Job. |
312	| **Detach Audio** | After a detach, the picture clip's own sound is off, and the sound is on its linked clip. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |
313	
314	If the clip plays but [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) or a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) has gone, check its speed. Both play only at normal speed, so a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without them.
315	
316	## An export won't start or stops
317	
318	An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file. An agent reads the same reason from `export_status`.
319	
320	While the timeline is empty, **File ▸ Export…** is greyed out. Add a clip first.
321	
322	"Preparing…" is a wait, not a stall. An export waits for what it has to draw and play first, such as speed-ramp audio, [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) masks, and sound measurements.
323	
324	| What you see | What to do |
325	| --- | --- |
326	| "Clip *N*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops. Wait for the clip's Status rows to show its loudness, then export again. |
327	| "Clip *N*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | A failed render keeps failing exports until you change the clip's timing or reopen Frame Job. |
328	| "The export was not started: the graphic…" or "The export was stopped at frame *N* of the graphic…" | Frame Job won't export a graphic that can't draw itself. Fix its [module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and export again. |
329	| "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose [another format](/export/formats/). |
330	| "An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is *N*." | Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate. An APNG has the same limit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/). |
331	| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) won't take a size of a different shape. Use a size from the popup, or one with the same proportions. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |
332	
333	A queued AV1 or VP9 job can sit waiting for memory, so it hasn't stalled. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
334	
335	:::caution
336	Quitting during an **Export…** progress sheet doesn't ask first, and it leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.
337	:::
338	
339	See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).
340	
341	## A feature asks for a key
342	
343	Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.
344	
345	| Message | What to do |
346	| --- | --- |
347	| "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." | Paste a key under **Transcription** in [Settings](/reference/settings/). |
348	| "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant." | Paste a key under **Assistant** in Settings. |
349	| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The key failed. Check it, and press **Verify** to test it. |
350	
351	A transcript made in one AssemblyAI region can't be seen from the other, so check **Region** too.
352	
353	An agent can't set a key, so a person has to. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
354	
355	## Recording won't start
356	
357	A recording needs macOS's permissions, and Frame Job asks for each one only when you press Record.
358	
359	- **Screen Recording** is at **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**. Once it's on, relaunch Frame Job, then press Record again. Later presses without it open that pane.
360	- **Microphone**, **Camera** and **Input Monitoring** are asked for only when the recording needs them.
361	- If you started Frame Job from a terminal or another app, macOS applies that app's permissions. The panel's note names the launching process and how to relaunch.
362	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
363	
364	An agent's `record_screen` never asks for a permission, so a person has to grant it first. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
365	
366	## An agent can't reach Frame Job
367	
368	Only programs running as you can connect, through the `framejob-mcp` helper inside the app.
369	
370	| What you see | What to do |
371	| --- | --- |
372	| The client can't start the helper after you moved Frame Job | In the **MCP** section of [Settings](/reference/settings/#mcp), press **Copy MCP Command** and register the new path. The path is the one you opened Settings from, and it doesn't follow the app. |
373	| "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." | The helper isn't in this copy. Use a complete copy of the app. |
374	| "Frame Job did not answer at…" | Frame Job launched but wasn't ready within 60 seconds. Later calls in that client session don't launch another copy, so quit the stray copy and try again. |
375	
376	See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

386	title: Glossary

388	---
389	
390	The words Frame Job uses, in plain terms, each with a link to the page that explains it.
391	
392	## Projects and the timeline
393	
394	- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
395	- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
396	- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
397	- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
398	- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
399	- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
400	- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
401	- **In/out range.** The span set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>, which many commands act on. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
402	- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
403	- **Media.** A file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab. Clips refer to it. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/).
404	- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
405	- **No-change edit, or identity.** An edit that was understood and had nothing to change. It beeps, makes no undo step and shows no message. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/#a-beep-with-no-message).
406	- **Package.** A `.framejob` project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
407	- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
408	- **Refusal.** A rule stopping an edit. Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's sentence after "Refused: " at the foot of the inspector. Nothing changes and no undo step is made. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
409	- **Ripple.** An edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
410	- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
411	- **Tick.** Frame Job's unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. The "Refused: " line and agent tools give lengths in ticks. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
412	- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).
413	
414	## Picture and sound
415	
416	- **Camera Log.** A file's setting saying which camera log curve it holds, so it's converted at the start of the picture. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
417	- **Cue.** One timed caption. See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).
418	- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
419	- **Deep.** A picture with more than 8 bits for each colour component. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
420	- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
421	- **Dynamic range.** Whether the project works in SDR or HDR (HLG). See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
422	- **J-cut and L-cut.** The sound of a linked pair starting before, or ending after, its picture. See [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
423	- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
424	- **LUFS.** The unit of loudness. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
425	- **LUT.** A colour lookup table in a `.cube` file. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
426	- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
427	- **Plate.** A clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from **Add Background**. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
428	- **Qualifier.** An adjustment clip's pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
429	- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
430	- **Scopes.** The waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram beside the preview. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
431	- **Slate.** What a clip draws in place of a picture it doesn't have, such as missing media. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
432	- **Stem.** One track's sound written as its own file beside the mix. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/).
433	- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
434	
435	## Graphics and agents
436	
437	- **Assistant.** The chat in the inspector that edits the open project on your own Anthropic key. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).
438	- **Category.** The list a module is filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
439	- **Error card.** What a graphic draws in its own box when it can't draw itself. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
440	- **Graphic.** A clip whose picture is drawn by code. It's the clip's content, not an effect. See [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
441	- **Graphic package.** A `.fjgraphic` file holding a module and the fonts and pictures it uses. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
442	- **Kept version.** An earlier text of a module the app kept, the last 10 for each module. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
443	- **MCP.** The protocol an agent uses to drive Frame Job, through the `framejob-mcp` helper. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
444	- **Module.** A graphic's source, one JavaScript module returning SVG for each frame. See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
445	- **Op.** Short for operation: one edit to a project, applied whole. Most agent tools each make one. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
446	- **Patch.** An object an agent sends holding only the properties it wants to change. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
447	- **Props.** The values a graphic is drawn with, stored on its clip. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/).
448	- **Template.** A module the app ships, copied into the package when you insert it. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
