674	title: "Pick from Canvas"
675	description: "Click a colour in the preview to centre an adjustment clip's qualifier on it, instead of finding it on the range strips."
676	---
677	
678	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
679	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
680	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
681	
682	Pick from Canvas aims a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) at a colour you can see. You click the picture and the ranges centre on that colour, so you don't have to find it on the strips by hand. The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/#pick-from-canvas) has an eyedropper of its own, with the same name.
683	
684	<AtAGlance
685	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas"
686	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
687	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
688	/>
689	
690	<Shot
691	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
692	  alt="The Qualifier section of the Color tab, with Hue ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30° and Soft 15°, Saturation ticked at Low 0.15, High 1.00 and Soft 0.05, Luma unticked, and the Pick from Canvas button beside a ticked Show Selection."
693	/>
694	
695	## Pick a colour
696	
697	<Steps>
698	
699	1. Select the [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), and move the playhead to a frame that shows the colour. The **Qualifier** section only appears while every selected clip is an adjustment clip. For any other selection the button beeps and no pick starts.
700	
701	2. In the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open the **Qualifier** section and press **Pick from Canvas**. The pointer becomes a crosshair over the preview, and a hint reads "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel".
702	
703	3. Click the colour in the preview.
704	
705	</Steps>
706	
707	The ranges move to that colour, and the pick ends. It's one undo step, named Qualifier.
708	
709	Frame Job reads the colour from the picture behind the adjustment clip, at the playhead. The clip's own grade and every layer in front of it are left out. So the colour you get is the one the qualifier will really test, even after your grade has changed how it looks, and clicking a title on top samples what's underneath it.
710	
711	Turn on [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) to check what the pick caught.
712	
713	## What a pick sets
714	
715	| Range | If it was off | If it was on |
716	| --- | --- | --- |
717	| **Hue** | Turns on, centred on the colour, 30° wide with 15° softness. | Moves its centre to the colour. |
718	| **Saturation** | Turns on, centred on the colour's saturation, 0.3 wide with softness 0.1. | Moves to centre on the colour's saturation. |
719	| **Luma** | Stays off. | Moves to centre on the colour's brightness. |
720	
721	A range that was already on keeps its width and softness, so you can set how wide you want a range and then pick again to move it. **Invert** and **Blur** don't change.
722	
723	If you click a near-grey, there's no real hue to aim at, so **Hue** turns off. A near-grey here is a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are less than 0.06 apart, on a scale of 0 to 1. **Saturation** still turns on and centres, which is how you pick the greys in a picture.
724	
725	**Saturation** and **Luma** stay inside 0 to 1. A range that would cross either end is shifted back inside at its full width, so it's no longer centred on the colour, but the colour stays inside it.
726	
727	## Pick inside an action
728	
729	With an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) selected, the picked ranges go to the action's end state instead of the clip, as any qualifier control does. The width and softness a range keeps are the ones the section is showing. Clicking a near-grey takes **Hue** out of the end state rather than turning it off, so if the clip itself has **Hue** on, it stays on. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
730	
731	## Cancel a pick
732	
733	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or press **Pick from Canvas** again. Changing the selection cancels the pick too. Nothing in the qualifier changes.
734	
735	A click in the area around the picture beeps and the pick stays on, so you can click again.
736	
737	## Good to know
738	
739	- Only one tool that waits for you on the preview can be on at a time. Starting Pick from Canvas cancels any other, such as the chroma key's eyedropper or a [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) drag, and starting one of those cancels a pick.
740	- If the playhead isn't on the adjustment clip, no layers are left out, so you sample the frame as it's drawn.
741	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) don't change what you sample. A pick reads the real picture, whatever the preview is showing.
742	- With several adjustment clips selected, Frame Job samples behind the first and writes the same ranges to all of them.
743	- In an HDR (HLG) project, a pick reads the HLG values, which are what the qualifier tests.
744	- If the selection changes while Frame Job is sampling, it beeps and changes nothing.
745	
746	## With an agent
747	
748	No agent tool clicks the canvas. An agent writes the ranges itself with `set_video`, or with `set_action_end` for an action's end state. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#qualifier).
749

758	title: "Waveform and RGB Parade"
759	description: "Read brightness and each colour channel across the frame, and find where highlights and shadows clip."
760	---
761	
762	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
763	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
764	
765	The Waveform shows how bright the picture is across the frame. The Parade shows the same thing for red, green and blue separately. Both tell you where the picture is clipping, which is hard to judge by eye.
766	
767	<AtAGlance
768	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
769	  keys="⌃⌘W"
770	  where="A slot's popup in the Scopes panel ▸ Waveform or Parade"
771	  tools="render_frame"
772	/>
773	
774	<Shot
775	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
776	  alt="The Waveform in the top slot of the Scopes panel beside the preview: a dark panel labelled 0, 50 and 100 at its left, with a white trace, red marks along its top and bottom edges, and under it the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %."
777	/>
778	
779	To see them, press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> to open the [Scopes](/color/scopes/) panel, then choose **Waveform** or **Parade** from a slot's popup. A new window's top slot is already on **Waveform**. Each takes 200 pt of height when the pane has room, and [shrinks to fit](/color/scopes/#when-the-pane-is-short) when it doesn't.
780	
781	In an HDR project they read differently, and [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) has the scale.
782	
783	## Read the waveform
784	
785	The Waveform plots the picture's luma (Y′, its brightness). Left to right in the scope is left to right across the frame, and height is brightness, with black at the bottom and white at the top. So a bright window on the left of the shot shows as a high patch on the left of the scope.
786	
787	Lines mark 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, with 0, 50 and 100 labelled at the left. The trace is white on a near-black background in both light and dark appearance. The brighter a point in the trace, the more pixels sit there, on a log scale, so a level only a few pixels reach still shows.
788	
789	## Read the RGB parade
790	
791	The Parade shows red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side, in that order, each tinted its own colour. Each one works like the Waveform, with the same lines and the whole width of the frame.
792	
793	Use it to see a colour cast. Something that should be neutral grey sits at the same height in all three, and a channel sitting higher or lower is pulling the picture toward or away from that colour. **Temperature** and **Tint** in [Light](/color/light/), and the [wheels](/color/wheels/), are the usual ways to bring them back in line.
794	
795	## Find clipping
796	
797	A pixel clips high at the top level, where an 8-bit file would write 255, and low at the bottom level, where it would write 0. Detail at those levels has gone flat.
798	
799	**Clip marks** are red marks on the top and bottom edges of the scope. A mark sits over every column where at least 0.5 % of the pixels clip, on the top edge for highlights and the bottom edge for shadows, so you can see where in the frame it's happening. The Parade marks each channel on its own, so one channel can clip when the others don't.
800	
801	**Readouts** under the Waveform give the share of the whole frame, for example **Highlights clipped 1.9 %** and **Shadows clipped 52.7 %**. They show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Histogram](/color/histogram/) has the same two readouts. The Parade and the Vectorscope have none.
802	
803	The readouts count everything in the frame. A black background around a smaller clip counts as clipped shadows, so a high figure may not be a problem with your footage. To bring highlights down, try **Exposure** or **Highlights** in [Light](/color/light/).
804	
805	## With an agent
806	
807	`render_frame` measures a frame's Waveform or Parade without the panel. Pass `waveform` or `parade` as true. Both are false by default. The tool's reply says what share of pixels clips high and low, and for the Parade it gives that for each channel, which the panel doesn't show as a number.
808	
809	A JSON file next to the image holds the raw counts, in 256 × 256 bins, with the clip marks and the clipping figures. It's named `<image path>.waveform.json` or `<image path>.parade.json`, and the Parade's holds red, green and blue separately. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram).
810

40	| **Tint** | −1 to +1 | Toward magenta or green |
41	| **Highlights** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the brighter half of the tones |
42	| **Shadows** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the darker half of the tones |
43	| **Whites** | −1 to +1 | Stretches the tones toward white, with black held |
44	| **Blacks** | −1 to +1 | Raises or deepens the dark end, with white held |
45	| **Vibrance** | −1 to +1 | Changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it |
46	| **Fade** | 0 to 1 | Lifts black and lowers white, for a washed-out film look |
47	
48	**Reset** in the header sets all nine back to 0 as one undo step, **Undo Light**, and leaves the [Color section](/color/color-section/) alone. The header reads "neutral" or "adjusted".
49	
50	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, every control here sets the value the action animates to, rather than the clip's own value.
51	
52	## Set the exposure
53	
54	**Exposure** brightens or darkens the picture in stops, from −3 to +3 EV. +1 doubles the light and −1 halves it.
55	
56	It works on linear light, meaning the amount of light in the scene rather than the encoded picture values, the way a camera's exposure does. So black stays black. To lift every level by the same amount, black included, use [Brightness](/color/color-section/#brightness).
57	
58	To judge exposure by measurement rather than by eye, watch the [waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) as you drag.
59	
60	## Set the white balance
61	
62	**Temperature** and **Tint** work on linear light, like Exposure. Both run from −1 to +1.
63	
64	| Control | Positive | Negative | At the limit |
65	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
66	| **Temperature** | Warmer: more red, less blue | Cooler: more blue, less red | At +1 red rises and blue falls by 0.3 of a stop. −1 is the reverse. |
67	| **Tint** | Toward magenta | Toward green | At +1 green falls by 0.3 of a stop, which reads as magenta. −1 raises it. |
68	
69	## Lift or lower the highlights and shadows
70	
71	**Highlights** moves the brighter half of the tones and **Shadows** the darker half. Both run from −1 to +1, and neither touches the other's half.
72	
73	At ±1 each moves its tones by up to a quarter of the full range. The move is strongest at the extreme, white for Highlights and black for Shadows, and fades to nothing at the middle of the tonal range.
74	
75	## Set the white and black points
76	
77	**Whites** stretches the tones toward white and holds black where it is. **Blacks** does the same at the other end: positive raises the dark end, negative deepens it, and white is held. Both run from −1 to +1.
78	
79	Each is a stretch of up to 15 %.
80	
81	## Add colour with Vibrance
82	
83	**Vibrance** changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it, from −1 to +1. Colours that are already strong are left mostly alone, which is the difference from [Saturation](/color/color-section/#saturation), which moves every colour alike.
84	
85	At +1 a nearly grey colour gets about twice its saturation, and at −1 it goes grey. A fully saturated colour doesn't change at either end.
86	
87	## Fade the picture
88	
89	**Fade** lifts black and lowers white for a washed-out film look. It runs from 0 to 1 and has no negative side. At 1, black rises to 10 % and white falls to 95 %.
90	
91	## With an agent
92	
93	One `set_video` call can set any of the nine Light controls and the four [Color](/color/color-section/) controls together, in its `color` object, and it leaves the ones it doesn't name alone. Each key is its control's name in lower case, such as `exposure` or `fade`, and 0 means no change. A positive `temperature` is warmer and a positive `tint` is more magenta. `set_action_end` takes the same keys for an action.
94	
95	A `set_video` call with a value outside a Light control's range fails, rather than being pulled back to the limit as a typed number is. `set_action_end` does take such a value, and the action stops at the limit when it's drawn. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#color).
96	
97	## Good to know
98	
99	- A number you type outside a control's range is pulled back to the nearest limit.
100	- Light acts after the Color section's four controls, even though the tab lists it first. See [The fixed grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order).
101	- On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), Light grades everything behind the clip.
102	- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), Exposure works on the scene's light as HLG encodes it, so +1 still doubles the light.

134	## The Wheels section
135	
136	<Steps>
137	
138	1. Select a video clip, an image, a still or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/). An adjustment clip's wheels grade everything behind it.
139	
140	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the Clip tab. See [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/) for which clips have it.
141	
142	3. Open **Wheels**. It starts closed, and its header reads **neutral** until a wheel moves, then **adjusted**.
143	
144	</Steps>
145	
146	Each of the three columns has a colour disc that [pushes its range toward a colour](#push-a-range-toward-a-colour), and a strip and a number field for [its brightness](#set-a-wheels-brightness). Every value starts at 0, which leaves the picture unchanged.
147	
148	The wheels apply after **Color** and **Light**, and before the [curves](/color/curves/) and the [look](/color/looks/). Their order is fixed.
149	
150	## What each wheel moves
151	
152	| Wheel | What it moves | Brightness at +1 | Brightness at −1 |
153	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
154	| **Lift** | Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. | Black rises to 25 %. | Everything below 20 % goes to black. |
155	| **Gamma** | Moves the middle tones and holds both ends. | A 50 % grey rises to about 71 %. | A 50 % grey falls to 25 %. |
156	| **Gain** | Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. | Every level is multiplied by 1.5. | Every level is halved, so white falls to 50 %. |
157	
158	A push follows the same rule. On **Lift** it tints the blacks and leaves white alone, and on **Gain** it tints the whites and leaves black alone.
159	
160	## Push a range toward a colour
161	
162	Press anywhere on a disc and drag. The direction you drag picks the hue, and the distance from the centre sets the strength. To warm the highlights, for example, drag **Gain**'s puck a little toward orange, between the red at the top of the disc and the yellow on its left.
163	
164	The square puck moves by however far the pointer moves. It doesn't jump to where you pressed, and a press with no drag changes nothing. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push, and past the rim the puck slides along the rim.
165	
166	A puck changes only that wheel's colour, never its brightness. One drag is one undo step, named after the wheel, such as **Undo Lift**.
167	
168	## Set a wheel's brightness
169	
170	The strip and the field under each disc set that wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1. The default is 0.
171	
172	- **Click the strip** off the knob and the value jumps there.
173	- **Drag the knob** and it moves from where it stands, with no jump.
174	- **Type in the field** for an exact value. It shows two decimals and has no unit. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves it, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps the old value. A number past either end is set to −1 or 1, and anything that isn't a number is ignored.
175	
176	A drag is one undo step and so is a typed value, each named after its wheel.
177	
178	## Make a fine adjustment
179	
180	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a puck or a strip to move at a tenth of the speed. On a strip, a press with <kbd>⌥</kbd> held moves the value relative to where it stands, with no jump.
181	
182	On a disc you can press or let go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> at any point in a drag. On a strip, letting go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> before the mouse sends the knob back under the pointer.
183	
184	The same key slows a point on a [curve](/color/curves/) and a handle on a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
185	
186	## Read the push
187	
188	Hover a disc to see its push as a hue angle and a strength, such as **Hue 34° · 0.25**. A centred puck reads **Neutral**.
189	
190	The angle counts from red at 0°, with green at 120° and blue at 240°. The strength runs from 0 at the centre to 1 at the rim. The push has no number field, so this is the only place in the inspector to read it as a number.
191	
192	## Wheels match the vectorscope
193	
194	Each disc is turned so that a hue sits where the [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) draws it. Dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward that colour.
195	
196	Red sits 103° counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock, just left of the top. Going counter-clockwise from there you'll find yellow on the left, green at the lower left, cyan near the bottom, blue on the right and magenta at the upper right. Every 75 % target on the vectorscope falls within about 12° of its place on the disc.
197	
198	## Reset the wheels
199	
200	| To reset | Do this |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| One wheel's push | Double-click its disc. The puck returns to the centre and the wheel's brightness stays. |
203	| One wheel's brightness | Double-click its strip. The value returns to 0 and the push stays. |
204	| All three wheels | Choose **Reset** in the section's header, or right-click the wheels and choose **Reset to default**. **Reset** appears once a wheel has moved, while no action is selected. |
205	
206	Each of these is one undo step, even when the first click of a double-click on the strip moved the knob. A double-click is named after its wheel, and resetting all three shows as **Undo Wheels**.
207	
208	## Grade several clips at once
209	
210	Select the clips and use the wheels as usual. Each control changes only its own values. A puck gives every selected clip that wheel's push and leaves each clip's brightness and other wheels alone. A strip or a field does the same for that wheel's brightness.
211	
212	The controls show the first clip's values. When the clips differ on any wheel, a **mixed** badge appears. One badge covers all three wheels.
213	
214	## Animate the wheels
215	
216	With an action selected, a puck, a strip or a field sets the action's end value, and the wheels ramp there from their values at the action's start. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
217	
218	While the action animates the wheels, a disc shows a hollow square at the start value and the puck in the action colour. A strip fills in the action colour from the start value. A coral mark shows the value under the playhead when it differs.
219	
220	The three wheels count as one row of the action. Moving any of them puts one [◆ in the gutter](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) beside all three, and removing the row takes all three out of the action. Right-click them for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**, or choose **Clear** in the section's header.
221	
222	## Good to know
223	
224	There's no Offset wheel. For an overall lift, use **Brightness** in the [Color section](/color/color-section/).
225	
226	## With an agent
227	
228	An agent can set the wheels with `set_video` as exact numbers, and an agent is the only way to enter a push by number. Each wheel takes a push as `x` and `y` and a brightness as `master`, all from −1 to 1. Its angles count the way the tooltip does, with red at 0° along positive `x`, and aren't turned to match the disc.
229	
230	Any wheel or value it leaves out stays as it is. Frame Job won't take a push past the rim from `set_video`, and says so rather than moving it to the rim. An action's end set with `set_action_end` is different: the value is kept, and the push stops at the rim while the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#wheels).
231

240	title: Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves
241	description: Turn one colour toward another, or saturate or mute it, without touching the rest of the picture.
242	---
243	
244	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
245	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
246	
247	The hue curves work on one colour at a time. **Hue** turns a chosen hue toward another, such as making the greens more teal. **Sat** saturates or mutes a chosen hue, such as calming a loud red. Both leave the other colours alone.
248	
249	<AtAGlance
250	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ the Hue and Sat cells"
251	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
252	/>
253	
254	## The two hue channels
255	
256	The **Hue** and **Sat** cells in the channel picker put the plot into degrees. Each channel lays the colours out across the plot, and its height says what happens to the colour at that position.
257	
258	| Cell | Curve | Across | Up | The centre line |
259	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
260	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue | Hue, 0° to 360° | A shift, −180° to +180° | 0°, no shift |
261	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat | Hue, 0° to 360° | A gain, 0× to 2× | 1×, unchanged |
262	
263	So a straight hue channel is a flat line across the middle, not a diagonal. It starts with two points on that line, at 0° and 180°.
264	
265	Points work as they do on any curve: click to add one, drag, nudge, type, delete and reset. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/#edit-points). A channel holds 2 to 16 points.
266	
267	The hue curves run after **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** and before the [look](/color/looks/), so they read each colour as those curves left it. Both hue curves read that colour once, before either changes it. A **Sat** point on the greens still acts on greens you've turned teal with **Hue**.
268	
269	## The spectrum strip
270	
271	A strip under the plot shows which colour each position stands for, from 0° at the left to 360° at the right. Thin lines mark every 60°, with lines across at the quarters and a stronger line at the centre.
272	
273	| Hue | Colour |
274	| --- | --- |
275	| 0° | Red |
276	| 60° | Yellow |
277	| 120° | Green |
278	| 180° | Cyan |
279	| 240° | Blue |
280	| 300° | Magenta |
281	
282	## Hue vs Hue
283	
284	A positive shift moves a colour to the right along the strip, from red toward yellow and green. A negative shift moves it to the left. Brightness stays as it was.
285	
286	To make the greens more teal:
287	
288	<Steps>
289	
290	1. Select the clip, open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open **Curves** and click the **Hue** cell.
291	
292	2. Click the plot at about 90° and again at about 150°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
293	
294	3. Press the centre line at about 120° and drag up. The label beside the pointer shows the shift, such as `Hue 120° → +30°`.
295	
296	</Steps>
297	
298	The outer points are saved with the first point you move. Without them, the shift spreads as far as the points at 0° and 180°.
299	
300	## Hue vs Sat
301	
302	Above the centre line a hue gets more saturated, and below it less. At the bottom of the plot, 0×, that hue goes grey. At the top, 2×, its saturation doubles. Saturation scales around the colour's own brightness.
303	
304	To mute the reds:
305	
306	<Steps>
307	
308	1. With **Curves** open on the clip, click the **Sat** cell.
309	
310	2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
311	
312	3. Drag the point at 0°, at the left end of the centre line, down. The label beside the pointer shows the gain, such as `Hue 0° → ×0.60`.
313	
314	</Steps>
315	
316	## Hue curve safeguards
317	
318	- **A grey stays grey.** A grey has no real hue to read, so a hue curve never tints it. When a colour's strongest and weakest channels are within 2% of each other it's left alone, and the effect fades in to full strength at 6%.
319	- **Points never cross the wrap.** A point stops at 0° and 359.9°, so it can't slide round to the other end. The curve itself does wrap: its right end runs on smoothly into its left end, so a shift around red covers both ends of the plot.
320	- **Colours stay in range.** When a turned colour can't keep its brightness, it gives up some saturation rather than clip.
321	
322	## Good to know
323	
324	- The closest a point gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.1°.
325	- **Reset Hue** and **Reset Sat** straighten one channel from the cell's right-click menu. The section's **Reset** straightens all six, the tone curves included. See [Reset curves](/color/curves/#reset-curves).
326	- The **Hue** slider in the [Color section](/color/color-section/) turns every colour at once. Hue vs Hue turns only the colours you choose.
327	- Hue curves animate inside an action as tone curves do. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
328	
329	## With an agent
330	
331	An agent writes `hue_hue` and `hue_sat` whole, each as a list of 2 to 16 hue and value pairs, and that list replaces the channel. It can place a point anywhere from 0 up to, but not including, 360. A value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#curves).
332

356	  name="05g-clip-curves.inspector"

359	
360	## The Curves section
361	
362	Select a video, image or still clip, or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) and open **Curves**. The section starts closed, and its header reads "neutral" until a curve changes, then "adjusted".
363	
364	The section has three parts, from top to bottom:
365	
366	- The channel picker, which chooses the curve you're editing.
367	- The plot, a square with a 4 × 4 grid. It grows with the inspector up to 300 pt wide.
368	- The selected point's **In** and **Out** fields, and **Delete**.
369	
370	Across the plot is the level going in, from 0 at the left to 1 at the right. Up the plot is the level coming out. A thin diagonal marks a straight curve, which changes nothing.
371	
372	## The channel picker
373	
374	Six cells above the plot choose the channel you edit. Click a different cell, and any selected point is deselected.
375	
376	| Cell | What it changes |
377	| --- | --- |
378	| **Master** | All three colours together. Use it for contrast and for the black and white points. |
379	| **Red** | The red channel only. |
380	| **Green** | The green channel only. |
381	| **Blue** | The blue channel only. |
382	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue, which turns a chosen hue toward another. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
383	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat, which saturates or mutes a chosen hue. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
384	
385	**Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** are the tone curves, and **Hue** and **Sat** are the hue curves.
386	
387	There's no separate luma curve. **Master** runs first, then each colour goes through its own channel, so a **Red** curve works on what **Master** has already done.
388

390	title: Filters
391	description: Stack up to four filters on a clip, from Blur and Pixelate to Sepia and Vignette, set how strong each one is, and animate them.
392	---
393	
394	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
395	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
396	
397	Filters change how a clip looks: soften it, break it into blocks, turn it black and white, darken its corners. A clip can carry up to four at once, and any clip that draws can have them, text, shapes and graphics included.
398	
399	<AtAGlance
400	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Filters"
401	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'paste_attributes']}
402	/>
403	
404	## Add a filter
405	
406	<Steps>
407	
408	1. Select the clip and open the **Clip** tab's [**Picture**](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab.
409	
410	2. Open the **Filters** section. On a clip with none it reads "No filters on this clip."
411	
412	3. Choose **Add Filter**. A Blur at 50 % joins the end of the stack.
413	
414	4. Pick the filter you want in the row's popup that reads **Blur**, and set its **Amount**.
415	
416	</Steps>
417	
418	Changing a filter's kind keeps its **Amount**. A clip can hold four, as the "4 at most" beside **Add Filter** says, and the button greys out at that point.
419	
420	Each change is one undo step. While the section is closed, its header shows `none`, the filter's name, or a count such as `3 filters`.
421	
422	## The seven filters
423	
424	| Filter | What it does | At 100 % |
425	| --- | --- | --- |
426	| **Blur** | Softens the picture. | A radius of 24 pixels |
427	| **Sharpen** | Crisps up edges and fine detail with an unsharp mask. | A gain of 2 |
428	| **Pixelate** | Breaks the picture into square blocks. The clip's edge and rounded corners stay clean. | Blocks 64 pixels across |
429	| **Sepia** | Gives the picture a warm old-photo tone. | The full tone |
430	| **Noir** | Turns the picture black and white and adds contrast. Taking **Saturation** to its lowest only removes the colour. | Fully black and white |
431	| **Vignette** | Darkens towards the edges in an ellipse fitted to the clip's cropped shape. The darkening starts a little under halfway from the centre to the corners. | Black corners |
432	| **Invert** | Turns the picture into its negative. | The full negative |
433	
434	Blur and Pixelate are measured in the clip's own pixels. Scale a clip up and the effect grows with it, and the same **Amount** looks finer on a 4K clip than on a 1080p one.
435	
436	## Set how strong a filter is
437	
438	**Amount** runs from 0 to 100 %, with quick picks at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. At 0 the filter stays on the clip and does nothing. Sepia, Noir and Invert mix from the original picture towards their full effect as the number rises.
439	
440	## Stack and reorder filters
441	
442	Each filter's row starts with a number popup, which is its place in the stack. Pick a different number to move the filter. You can't drag rows. A move is one undo step.
443	
444	The place doesn't decide everything, because Frame Job always works through a stack in this order:
445	
446	1. Pixelate, whatever its place.
447	2. The **Color** section of the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/): **Brightness**, **Contrast**, **Saturation** and **Hue**.
448	3. Blur and Sharpen, whatever their places.
449	4. The rest of the Color tab: **Light**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look**.
450	5. Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert, in the order of their places.
451	
452	So the order only changes the picture among Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert. Noir then Sepia gives a warm black and white, while Sepia then Noir gives a plain one. Moving a Blur above or below a Sepia changes nothing.
453	
454	Filters of the same kind combine:
455	
456	| In one stack | You get |
457	| --- | --- |
458	| Two Blurs | One wider blur. Two at 100 % reach a radius of about 34 pixels, and four reach 48. |
459	| Two Sharpens | The sum of the two. |
460	| Two Pixelates | The coarser of the two. |
461	
462	## Remove a filter
463	
464	Choose **Remove** in the filter's row. **Reset** in the section's header takes off the whole stack, and it's there only while no action is selected.
465	
466	## Animate a filter
467	
468	An [action](/motion/actions/) can ramp a filter's **Amount**, for example a blur that builds across a clip.
469	
470	<Steps>
471	
472	1. Add the filter and set **Amount** to where the ramp should start.
473	
474	2. Add an action on the clip and keep it selected.
475	
476	3. Set **Amount** to where the ramp should end.
477	
478	</Steps>
479	
480	With an action selected, each control does something different:
481	
482	| You change | What happens |
483	| --- | --- |
484	| **Amount** | It ramps across the action. |
485	| The filter's kind | It switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end". The other filters keep ramping. |
486	| The filter's place | It moves at the action's end. |
487	| **Add Filter** or **Remove** | It changes the clip itself rather than the action, so it isn't animated. |
488	
489	:::caution
490	Adding or removing a filter while an action already animates the stack leaves the two stacks different lengths. The action stops ramping them and the filters switch at its end instead. To get the ramp back, select the action, choose **Clear** in the section's header, then set the clip's amounts and the action's again.
491	:::
492	
493	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how the rows behave in an action.
494	
495	## Filters on an adjustment clip
496	
497	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no **Picture** sub-tab, so it can't take a filter from the inspector. It gets one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) instead.
498	
499	<Steps>
500	
501	1. Put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert on an ordinary clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
502	
503	2. Select the adjustment clip.
504	
505	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
506	
507	</Steps>
508	
509	The filter then applies to everything behind the adjustment clip for as long as it lasts, and to nothing on a track in front.
510	
511	Blur, Sharpen and Pixelate can't go on an adjustment clip, because it has no picture of its own to sample. Pasting from a clip that has one stops with an error naming the clip and the filter, and changes nothing.
512	
513	:::caution
514	Paste Attributes replaces the target's picture settings, not only its filters. Pasting onto an adjustment clip overwrites its grade and its Strength with the copied clip's, so paste first and grade afterwards.
515	:::
516	
517	## Good to know
518	
519	- A filter covers the whole picture for the whole clip. To blur or pixelate one region, such as a face, use [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
520	- With several clips selected, the rows show the first clip's stack, and any edit gives every selected clip that whole stack.
521	- A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the Filters section, but a filter on it has no effect. Put filters on the clips inside the nest.
522	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), a clip's filters shape the cut it makes. **Alpha** and **Inverted Alpha** read only transparency, so Sharpen, Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert change nothing there.
523	- A clip's [reflection](/effects/reflection/) shows its filters too.
524	
525	## With an agent
526	
527	An agent sets a clip's filters with `set_video`, as a list of kinds and amounts, with each amount from 0 to 1. The list replaces the old one whole, so it sends every filter it wants to keep, and an empty list clears the stack. A fifth filter is an error, and nothing changes. It can put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert straight onto an adjustment clip, with no paste. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#filters).
528	
529	With `set_action_end`, an agent can give an action a list of a different length, which switches at the action's end rather than ramping. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).

content.content:
---
title: "The Preview Window"
description: Show the picture in a second window with no handles or guides, on another display or full screen.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Preview Window shows the picture on its own, with no handles or guides over it. Use it to put the picture on a second display while you edit in the main window.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Window" keys="⇧⌘P" />

## Open the Preview Window

Press <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd> or choose **View ▸ Preview Window**. The same key hides it again, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's open. It opens on an empty timeline too, where the window is black.

The window is titled after the project, for example "Intro — Preview", and has a black surround. You can resize it down to 320 × 200, and it can go full screen.

It uses the same player as the main preview, so the two never drift apart. [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection** and **Show SDR Version** all apply to it, but the [corner tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags) don't appear in it.

The window is only for looking. Safe-area guides, zoom and the handles for moving clips stay in the main preview.

## Remembered position

The window remembers its position and size between launches, so it opens where you last left it, on a second display for example. The first time, it opens at 640 × 360 in the middle of the screen. It stays visible when you switch to another app.

It closes with its project window. Whether it's open isn't remembered, so it starts off in each new window.

## Keys

The window doesn't take you away from the editor. While it has the focus:

- Playback keys work: <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd>, <kbd>L</kbd>, the arrows, Home and End.
- The editor's other single-letter keys work too, such as <kbd>M</kbd> for a marker or <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> for the range.
- Every editor ⌘ command works, so <kbd>⌘E</kbd> opens the export sheet and <kbd>⌘T</kbd> splits.
- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> undoes the project's last step, and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> redoes it, the same steps as in the editor.
- <kbd>⌘W</kbd> closes the Preview Window, not the project.

Single-letter keys stop while a field in the editor window is being edited, or while the editor has a sheet open.

## Good to know

- There's one saved position for every project. With two projects' Preview Windows open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved to.
- The window isn't listed in the **Window** menu. Use **View ▸ Preview Window** to find it.
- After you save a project under a new name, the title updates the next time you show the window.

## Related

- [The preview](/timeline/preview/)
- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
- [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/)
---
title: "Canvas background and timecode"
description: "Set the colour behind every layer, make the canvas transparent, choose how times are shown, and decide how new clips are sized."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) sets three things for the whole project: the colour behind your clips, how times are written, and how big a new clip starts.

<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Appearance" tools={['set_canvas', 'add_clip']} />

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background** | The colour behind every layer. | Black, opaque |
| **Timecode** | How the project shows a time. | Frames |
| **Fit new clips to canvas** | Scales down a new clip that's bigger than the canvas. | On |

A change to **Timecode** or **Fit new clips to canvas** is one undo step.

## Set the background colour

Click the **Background** swatch and pick a colour in the Colors panel. The colour sits behind every layer, so it shows wherever no clip covers the canvas.

To put a colour on the timeline as a clip instead, see [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).

## Make the background transparent

Lower the opacity in the Colors panel. The swatch shows a checkerboard behind the colour, and the **Background** row of the [Document summary](/projects/document-tab/#the-document-summary) reads `Transparent`, or the colour with its opacity.

Most export formats can't carry transparency, so while the background isn't fully opaque, the section adds a note about the formats that can.

| The note says | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." | Three or more formats keep it, so the note counts them. They're HEVC with Alpha (MOV), VP9 with Alpha (WebM), ProRes 4444 (MOV) and Animated PNG. |
| "Transparent — needs an alpha format." | Frame Job can't name the formats yet, which can happen on a project with nothing on the timeline. |

See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).

## Choose a timecode format

**Timecode** sets how times are written everywhere the project shows one, including the toolbar, the ruler, the inspector, markers and the transcript.

| Choice | Looks like |
| --- | --- |
| **Frames** | `HH:MM:SS:FF` |
| **Milliseconds** | `HH:MM:SS.mmm` |

**Frames** doesn't drop frames, so at 29.97 fps the count runs slightly behind the clock over a long timeline.

## Fit new clips to canvas

This decides how big a new clip starts. It's on by default.

| Setting | A clip bigger than the canvas | Any other clip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On | Starts at Fit scale: scaled down until all of it shows. | Starts at 100 %, its native size. |
| Off | Starts at 100 %, so it runs past the edges of the canvas. | Starts at 100 %. |

A clip counts as bigger when either its width or its height is larger than the canvas. Fit never scales a clip up, and changing the setting leaves clips already on the timeline as they are. To fit or fill one clip, see [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/).

## Reset the section

**Reset** on the **Appearance** header puts all three back to their defaults: opaque black, **Frames** and on. It's offered only while one of them differs, and it's one undo step.

## With an agent

[`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas) sets all three, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value.

| Argument | What it takes |
| --- | --- |
| `background` | Four numbers from 0 to 1, `[r, g, b, a]`. Three numbers, or one outside the range, fails and nothing changes. |
| `timecode_frames` | `true` for **Frames**, `false` for **Milliseconds**. |
| `fit_new_clips` | `true` or `false`, as the checkbox. |

[`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_clip) follows **Fit new clips to canvas** as the app does. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).

## Related

- [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/)
- [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/)
- [Image clips](/text-and-shapes/image-clips/)
- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)
---
title: "Burn in timecode"
description: Draw the project's timecode into an exported picture, so a reviewer's notes point at exact frames.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Burn in timecode draws the project's timecode into the exported picture. Use it for a review copy, so a note about a frame carries the number you'll find on your timeline.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Burn in timecode"
  tools={['export', 'render_frame']}
/>

## Burn in timecode

Choose **File ▸ Export…** and turn on **Burn in timecode**. It's off by default.

The timecode appears only in the exported file, never in the preview. It sits centred near the bottom of the picture, on a translucent black plate, on top of everything, captions included.

The box works on every format with a picture, Animated GIF and Animated PNG included. It's greyed out for the audio-only formats, and **File ▸ Save Frame…** never offers it.

The sheet remembers it with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## What the timecode shows

It uses the project's own timecode format, as the toolbar shows it: `HH:MM:SS:FF` or `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, non-drop. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

It shows **project time**. A file exported from an [in/out range](/export/range/) that starts at 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 in a player, but its first frame reads 00:00:10:00. That's the number a reviewer's note needs.

## With an agent

`burn_in_timecode` turns it on in `export`, and it's off by default. `render_frame` takes the same argument, so an agent can draw the timecode into a single frame, which **Save Frame…** can't do. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)
---
title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
/>

## Repackage or convert a file

<Steps>

1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."

2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.

3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.

</Steps>

The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:

| The button | What the alert tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |

If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.

A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.

## What's copied and what's re-encoded

Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.

| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
| Sound | AAC, ALAC and the usual 16-, 24- and 32-bit PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |

The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.

VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. Frame Job then checks that every frame of the copy sits exactly on the frame rate. If the copy fails that check, or won't open, it's re-encoded to H.264 once. Unless you've told Frame Job to do this automatically, it asks you again first.

Only the first video stream and the first audio stream are carried over. Subtitles and data streams are dropped.

560	
561	## Confine it to part of the picture
562	
563	An adjustment clip grades the whole frame behind it. There are two ways to narrow that:
564	
565	- **To an area:** put a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) directly in front of the adjustment clip's track. On a track cut by a matte, the clip grades only inside the matte. The matte cuts everything on that track, so keep other clips off it.
566	- **To a colour or brightness:** set a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/). It picks pixels by hue, saturation and luma.
567	
568	The two work together. The grade reaches only the pixels both allow, mixed at the clip's Strength.
569	
570	The adjustment clip must not sit on the matte track itself. There it has no effect, and the inspector says "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect."
571	
572	## Grade a graphic
573	
574	[Graphics](/graphics/graphic-tab/) have no **Color** sub-tab, and neither do text, shapes or nests. To grade one, put an adjustment clip above it for the span you want. Select the clip first and **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** matches its span, unless an In–Out range is set. The adjustment clip grades every track behind it, so add a matte if other tracks show through.
575	
576	## Limits
577	
578	### No nests
579	
580	An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest. **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out while one is open, Frame Job won't [nest](/editing/nests/) a selection that holds an adjustment clip, and pasting one into an open nest fails. Inside a nest it would grade the layers behind the nest clip as well as the nest's own.
581	
582	To grade a nest, put an adjustment clip above the nest clip on the timeline.
583	
584	### No transitions or overlaps
585	
586	An adjustment clip can't take a [transition](/motion/transitions/), and it can't overlap another clip on its track, because an overlap is a transition. Frame Job won't make the edit, so [fade its Strength](#fade-the-grade-in-or-out) instead. Two clips that only touch are fine.
587	
588	### No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes
589	
590	These need pixels or a colour of the clip's own, and an adjustment clip has neither. If [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) would bring one onto an adjustment clip, nothing is pasted.
591	
592	The point [filters](/effects/filters/), **Sepia**, **Noir**, **Vignette** and **Invert**, do work, and apply to the picture behind it. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so they reach it through Paste Attributes or an agent.
593	
594	## Good to know
595	
596	- A clip with no grade set changes nothing, and neither does a qualifier on its own. A qualifier narrows a grade, so there has to be one.
597	- **Clip ▸ Speed…**, **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** and **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** are dimmed for an adjustment clip, and its **Clip** sub-tab has no [Speed](/speed/speed-section/) section, because it has no source and no picture size. [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) still stretches or squeezes one inside its range.
598	
599	## With an agent
600	
601	`add_adjustment_clip` places a clip on the `track` and `at` the time you name, and it lasts 5 seconds unless you give a `duration`. It doesn't work out a span or a track as the menu does, so an agent can put one on a matte track, where it does nothing. It won't add one while a nest is open.
602	
603	`set_video` then grades it with everything the Color tab offers, and can also give it point filters directly. To an agent, Strength is the clip's `opacity`, from 0 to 1, and `set_action_end` animates it. A blur, sharpen or pixelate filter or a blend mode is an error, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter". See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_adjustment_clip) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#on-an-adjustment-clip).
604	
605	## Related
606	
607	- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
608	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
609	- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
610	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
611	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
612	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
613	---
614	title: Qualifiers
615	description: Limit an adjustment clip's grade to the pixels of one colour or brightness, using hue, saturation and luma ranges.
616	---
617	
618	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
619	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
620	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
621	
622	A qualifier limits an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/)'s grade to the pixels behind it that match up to three ranges of hue, saturation and luma. Use it to change one colour and leave the rest of the picture alone.
623	
624	<AtAGlance
625	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier"
626	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'render_frame']}
627	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
628	/>
629	
630	<Shot
631	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
632	  alt="The Qualifier section of an adjustment clip, its header reading hue · sat. Hue is ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30°, Soft 15°, and Saturation at Low 0.15, High 1.00, Soft 0.05. Each strip is dimmed outside its range. Luma is unticked, with a dimmed strip and greyed-out fields. Below are Invert, Blur at 0%, the Pick from Canvas button and a ticked Show Selection."
633	/>
634	
635	## Grade one colour
636	
637	<Steps>
638	
639	1. Put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) above the picture, for the span you want.
640	
641	2. With the clip selected, give it a grade in the **Color** sub-tab. A qualifier on its own changes nothing, because it only narrows a grade.
642	
643	3. Open the **Qualifier** section by clicking its header if it's [closed](/getting-started/inspector/#fold-a-section). Press **Pick from Canvas** and click the colour in the preview, or tick a range and set it by hand.
644	
645	4. Tick **Show Selection** to see what's picked. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
646	
647	5. Adjust the ranges until the selection is clean, then untick **Show Selection**.
648	
649	</Steps>
650	
651	A qualifier reaches every track behind the clip. To keep it to one area as well, [add a matte](/color/adjustment-clips/#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).
652	
653	## The Qualifier section
654	
655	The **Qualifier** section appears only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip, right after **Adjustment**. A picture clip can't have a qualifier.
656	
657	It holds the three ranges, then **Invert**, **Blur**, [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
658	
659	Matching reads the picture behind the clip as it was before the grade, so the grade never changes what it selects.
660	
661	### The Qualifier summary
662	
663	The section's header says what's set: the ranges that are on, then `inverted`, then the blur. For example, `hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%`. It reads `off` when nothing is set.
664	
665	**Reset** appears once anything is set, as long as no action is selected. It turns all three ranges off, clears **Invert** and sets **Blur** to 0 %, as one undo step named **Qualifier**.
666	
667	## Turn a range on
668	
669	Each range has a checkbox, a strip and three fields. Tick the checkbox and the range starts at its default. Ticking or unticking is one undo step named after the range.
670	
671	A range that's off has a dimmed strip that ignores presses, and greyed-out fields, so tick it first. Unticking forgets the range's values: tick it again and it's back at its default.
672	
673	---
674	title: "Pick from Canvas"
675	description: "Click a colour in the preview to centre an adjustment clip's qualifier on it, instead of finding it on the range strips."
676	---
677	
678	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
679	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
680	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
681	
682	Pick from Canvas aims a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) at a colour you can see. You click the picture and the ranges centre on that colour, so you don't have to find it on the strips by hand. The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/#pick-from-canvas) has an eyedropper of its own, with the same name.
683	
684	<AtAGlance
685	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas"
686	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
687	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
688	/>
689	
690	<Shot
691	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
692	  alt="The Qualifier section of the Color tab, with Hue ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30° and Soft 15°, Saturation ticked at Low 0.15, High 1.00 and Soft 0.05, Luma unticked, and the Pick from Canvas button beside a ticked Show Selection."
693	/>
694	
695	## Pick a colour
696	
697	<Steps>
698	
699	1. Select the [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), and move the playhead to a frame that shows the colour. The **Qualifier** section only appears while every selected clip is an adjustment clip. For any other selection the button beeps and no pick starts.
700	
701	2. In the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open the **Qualifier** section and press **Pick from Canvas**. The pointer becomes a crosshair over the preview, and a hint reads "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel".
702	
703	3. Click the colour in the preview.
704	
705	</Steps>
706	
707	The ranges move to that colour, and the pick ends. It's one undo step, named Qualifier.
708	
709	Frame Job reads the colour from the picture behind the adjustment clip, at the playhead. The clip's own grade and every layer in front of it are left out. So the colour you get is the one the qualifier will really test, even after your grade has changed how it looks, and clicking a title on top samples what's underneath it.
710	
711	Turn on [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) to check what the pick caught.
712	
713	## What a pick sets
714	
715	| Range | If it was off | If it was on |
716	| --- | --- | --- |
717	| **Hue** | Turns on, centred on the colour, 30° wide with 15° softness. | Moves its centre to the colour. |
718	| **Saturation** | Turns on, centred on the colour's saturation, 0.3 wide with softness 0.1. | Moves to centre on the colour's saturation. |
719	| **Luma** | Stays off. | Moves to centre on the colour's brightness. |
720	
721	A range that was already on keeps its width and softness, so you can set how wide you want a range and then pick again to move it. **Invert** and **Blur** don't change.
722	
723	If you click a near-grey, there's no real hue to aim at, so **Hue** turns off. A near-grey here is a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are less than 0.06 apart, on a scale of 0 to 1. **Saturation** still turns on and centres, which is how you pick the greys in a picture.
724	
725	**Saturation** and **Luma** stay inside 0 to 1. A range that would cross either end is shifted back inside at its full width, so it's no longer centred on the colour, but the colour stays inside it.
726	
727	## Pick inside an action
728	
729	With an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) selected, the picked ranges go to the action's end state instead of the clip, as any qualifier control does. The width and softness a range keeps are the ones the section is showing. Clicking a near-grey takes **Hue** out of the end state rather than turning it off, so if the clip itself has **Hue** on, it stays on. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
730	
731	## Cancel a pick
732	
733	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or press **Pick from Canvas** again. Changing the selection cancels the pick too. Nothing in the qualifier changes.
734	
735	A click in the area around the picture beeps and the pick stays on, so you can click again.
736	
737	## Good to know
738	
739	- Only one tool that waits for you on the preview can be on at a time. Starting Pick from Canvas cancels any other, such as the chroma key's eyedropper or a [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) drag, and starting one of those cancels a pick.
740	- If the playhead isn't on the adjustment clip, no layers are left out, so you sample the frame as it's drawn.
741	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) don't change what you sample. A pick reads the real picture, whatever the preview is showing.
742	- With several adjustment clips selected, Frame Job samples behind the first and writes the same ranges to all of them.
743	- In an HDR (HLG) project, a pick reads the HLG values, which are what the qualifier tests.
744	- If the selection changes while Frame Job is sampling, it beeps and changes nothing.
745	
746	## With an agent
747	
748	No agent tool clicks the canvas. An agent writes the ranges itself with `set_video`, or with `set_action_end` for an action's end state. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#qualifier).
749

758	title: "Waveform and RGB Parade"
759	description: "Read brightness and each colour channel across the frame, and find where highlights and shadows clip."
760	---
761	
762	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
763	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
764	
765	The Waveform shows how bright the picture is across the frame. The Parade shows the same thing for red, green and blue separately. Both tell you where the picture is clipping, which is hard to judge by eye.
766	
767	<AtAGlance
768	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
769	  keys="⌃⌘W"
770	  where="A slot's popup in the Scopes panel ▸ Waveform or Parade"
771	  tools="render_frame"
772	/>
773	
774	<Shot
775	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
776	  alt="The Waveform in the top slot of the Scopes panel beside the preview: a dark panel labelled 0, 50 and 100 at its left, with a white trace, red marks along its top and bottom edges, and under it the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %."
777	/>
778	
779	To see them, press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> to open the [Scopes](/color/scopes/) panel, then choose **Waveform** or **Parade** from a slot's popup. A new window's top slot is already on **Waveform**. Each takes 200 pt of height when the pane has room, and [shrinks to fit](/color/scopes/#when-the-pane-is-short) when it doesn't.
780	
781	In an HDR project they read differently, and [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) has the scale.
782	
783	## Read the waveform
784	
785	The Waveform plots the picture's luma (Y′, its brightness). Left to right in the scope is left to right across the frame, and height is brightness, with black at the bottom and white at the top. So a bright window on the left of the shot shows as a high patch on the left of the scope.
786	
787	Lines mark 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, with 0, 50 and 100 labelled at the left. The trace is white on a near-black background in both light and dark appearance. The brighter a point in the trace, the more pixels sit there, on a log scale, so a level only a few pixels reach still shows.
788	
789	## Read the RGB parade
790	
791	The Parade shows red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side, in that order, each tinted its own colour. Each one works like the Waveform, with the same lines and the whole width of the frame.
792	
793	Use it to see a colour cast. Something that should be neutral grey sits at the same height in all three, and a channel sitting higher or lower is pulling the picture toward or away from that colour. **Temperature** and **Tint** in [Light](/color/light/), and the [wheels](/color/wheels/), are the usual ways to bring them back in line.
794	
795	## Find clipping
796	
797	A pixel clips high at the top level, where an 8-bit file would write 255, and low at the bottom level, where it would write 0. Detail at those levels has gone flat.
798	
799	**Clip marks** are red marks on the top and bottom edges of the scope. A mark sits over every column where at least 0.5 % of the pixels clip, on the top edge for highlights and the bottom edge for shadows, so you can see where in the frame it's happening. The Parade marks each channel on its own, so one channel can clip when the others don't.
800	
801	**Readouts** under the Waveform give the share of the whole frame, for example **Highlights clipped 1.9 %** and **Shadows clipped 52.7 %**. They show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Histogram](/color/histogram/) has the same two readouts. The Parade and the Vectorscope have none.
802	
803	The readouts count everything in the frame. A black background around a smaller clip counts as clipped shadows, so a high figure may not be a problem with your footage. To bring highlights down, try **Exposure** or **Highlights** in [Light](/color/light/).
804	
805	## With an agent
806	
807	`render_frame` measures a frame's Waveform or Parade without the panel. Pass `waveform` or `parade` as true. Both are false by default. The tool's reply says what share of pixels clips high and low, and for the Parade it gives that for each channel, which the panel doesn't show as a number.
808	
809	A JSON file next to the image holds the raw counts, in 256 × 256 bins, with the clip marks and the clipping figures. It's named `<image path>.waveform.json` or `<image path>.parade.json`, and the Parade's holds red, green and blue separately. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram).
810	
811	## Related
812	
813	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
814	- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
815	- [Histogram](/color/histogram/)
816	- [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/)
817	- [Light](/color/light/)
818

40	| **Tint** | −1 to +1 | Toward magenta or green |
41	| **Highlights** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the brighter half of the tones |
42	| **Shadows** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the darker half of the tones |
43	| **Whites** | −1 to +1 | Stretches the tones toward white, with black held |
44	| **Blacks** | −1 to +1 | Raises or deepens the dark end, with white held |
45	| **Vibrance** | −1 to +1 | Changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it |
46	| **Fade** | 0 to 1 | Lifts black and lowers white, for a washed-out film look |
47	
48	**Reset** in the header sets all nine back to 0 as one undo step, **Undo Light**, and leaves the [Color section](/color/color-section/) alone. The header reads "neutral" or "adjusted".
49	
50	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, every control here sets the value the action animates to, rather than the clip's own value.
51	
52	## Set the exposure
53	
54	**Exposure** brightens or darkens the picture in stops, from −3 to +3 EV. +1 doubles the light and −1 halves it.
55	
56	It works on linear light, meaning the amount of light in the scene rather than the encoded picture values, the way a camera's exposure does. So black stays black. To lift every level by the same amount, black included, use [Brightness](/color/color-section/#brightness).
57	
58	To judge exposure by measurement rather than by eye, watch the [waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) as you drag.
59	
60	## Set the white balance
61	
62	**Temperature** and **Tint** work on linear light, like Exposure. Both run from −1 to +1.
63	
64	| Control | Positive | Negative | At the limit |
65	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
66	| **Temperature** | Warmer: more red, less blue | Cooler: more blue, less red | At +1 red rises and blue falls by 0.3 of a stop. −1 is the reverse. |
67	| **Tint** | Toward magenta | Toward green | At +1 green falls by 0.3 of a stop, which reads as magenta. −1 raises it. |
68	
69	## Lift or lower the highlights and shadows
70	
71	**Highlights** moves the brighter half of the tones and **Shadows** the darker half. Both run from −1 to +1, and neither touches the other's half.
72	
73	At ±1 each moves its tones by up to a quarter of the full range. The move is strongest at the extreme, white for Highlights and black for Shadows, and fades to nothing at the middle of the tonal range.
74	
75	## Set the white and black points
76	
77	**Whites** stretches the tones toward white and holds black where it is. **Blacks** does the same at the other end: positive raises the dark end, negative deepens it, and white is held. Both run from −1 to +1.
78	
79	Each is a stretch of up to 15 %.
80	
81	## Add colour with Vibrance
82	
83	**Vibrance** changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it, from −1 to +1. Colours that are already strong are left mostly alone, which is the difference from [Saturation](/color/color-section/#saturation), which moves every colour alike.
84	
85	At +1 a nearly grey colour gets about twice its saturation, and at −1 it goes grey. A fully saturated colour doesn't change at either end.
86	
87	## Fade the picture
88	
89	**Fade** lifts black and lowers white for a washed-out film look. It runs from 0 to 1 and has no negative side. At 1, black rises to 10 % and white falls to 95 %.
90	
91	## With an agent
92	
93	One `set_video` call can set any of the nine Light controls and the four [Color](/color/color-section/) controls together, in its `color` object, and it leaves the ones it doesn't name alone. Each key is its control's name in lower case, such as `exposure` or `fade`, and 0 means no change. A positive `temperature` is warmer and a positive `tint` is more magenta. `set_action_end` takes the same keys for an action.
94	
95	A `set_video` call with a value outside a Light control's range fails, rather than being pulled back to the limit as a typed number is. `set_action_end` does take such a value, and the action stops at the limit when it's drawn. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#color).
96	
97	## Good to know
98	
99	- A number you type outside a control's range is pulled back to the nearest limit.
100	- Light acts after the Color section's four controls, even though the tab lists it first. See [The fixed grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order).
101	- On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), Light grades everything behind the clip.
102	- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), Exposure works on the scene's light as HLG encodes it, so +1 still doubles the light.
103

113	title: "Wheels"
114	description: "Balance a clip's shadows, middle tones and highlights with Lift, Gamma and Gain, pushing each toward a colour and setting its brightness."
115	---
116	
117	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
118	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
119	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
120	
121	The wheels balance a picture by tone. **Lift** works on the shadows, **Gamma** on the middle tones and **Gain** on the highlights, so you can cool the shadows, warm the highlights or take a colour cast out of one part of the picture.
122	
123	<AtAGlance
124	  keys={['⌥-drag', 'Double-click']}
125	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Wheels"
126	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
127	/>
128	
129	<Shot
130	  name="05f-clip-wheels.inspector"
131	  alt="The Wheels section of the Color tab, reading adjusted, with a Reset button. Three columns, Lift, Gamma and Gain, each hold a colour disc, a strip and a number field. Lift's puck is pushed up and to the left, toward red-orange, and its field reads 0.10. Gamma is centred at 0.00. Gain's puck is centred and its field reads 0.20."
132	/>
133	
134	## The Wheels section
135	
136	<Steps>
137	
138	1. Select a video clip, an image, a still or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/). An adjustment clip's wheels grade everything behind it.
139	
140	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the Clip tab. See [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/) for which clips have it.
141	
142	3. Open **Wheels**. It starts closed, and its header reads **neutral** until a wheel moves, then **adjusted**.
143	
144	</Steps>
145	
146	Each of the three columns has a colour disc that [pushes its range toward a colour](#push-a-range-toward-a-colour), and a strip and a number field for [its brightness](#set-a-wheels-brightness). Every value starts at 0, which leaves the picture unchanged.
147	
148	The wheels apply after **Color** and **Light**, and before the [curves](/color/curves/) and the [look](/color/looks/). Their order is fixed.
149	
150	## What each wheel moves
151	
152	| Wheel | What it moves | Brightness at +1 | Brightness at −1 |
153	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
154	| **Lift** | Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. | Black rises to 25 %. | Everything below 20 % goes to black. |
155	| **Gamma** | Moves the middle tones and holds both ends. | A 50 % grey rises to about 71 %. | A 50 % grey falls to 25 %. |
156	| **Gain** | Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. | Every level is multiplied by 1.5. | Every level is halved, so white falls to 50 %. |
157	
158	A push follows the same rule. On **Lift** it tints the blacks and leaves white alone, and on **Gain** it tints the whites and leaves black alone.
159	
160	## Push a range toward a colour
161	
162	Press anywhere on a disc and drag. The direction you drag picks the hue, and the distance from the centre sets the strength. To warm the highlights, for example, drag **Gain**'s puck a little toward orange, between the red at the top of the disc and the yellow on its left.
163	
164	The square puck moves by however far the pointer moves. It doesn't jump to where you pressed, and a press with no drag changes nothing. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push, and past the rim the puck slides along the rim.
165	
166	A puck changes only that wheel's colour, never its brightness. One drag is one undo step, named after the wheel, such as **Undo Lift**.
167	
168	## Set a wheel's brightness
169	
170	The strip and the field under each disc set that wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1. The default is 0.
171	
172	- **Click the strip** off the knob and the value jumps there.
173	- **Drag the knob** and it moves from where it stands, with no jump.
174	- **Type in the field** for an exact value. It shows two decimals and has no unit. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves it, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps the old value. A number past either end is set to −1 or 1, and anything that isn't a number is ignored.
175	
176	A drag is one undo step and so is a typed value, each named after its wheel.
177	
178	## Make a fine adjustment
179	
180	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a puck or a strip to move at a tenth of the speed. On a strip, a press with <kbd>⌥</kbd> held moves the value relative to where it stands, with no jump.
181	
182	On a disc you can press or let go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> at any point in a drag. On a strip, letting go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> before the mouse sends the knob back under the pointer.
183	
184	The same key slows a point on a [curve](/color/curves/) and a handle on a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
185	
186	## Read the push
187	
188	Hover a disc to see its push as a hue angle and a strength, such as **Hue 34° · 0.25**. A centred puck reads **Neutral**.
189	
190	The angle counts from red at 0°, with green at 120° and blue at 240°. The strength runs from 0 at the centre to 1 at the rim. The push has no number field, so this is the only place in the inspector to read it as a number.
191	
192	## Wheels match the vectorscope
193	
194	Each disc is turned so that a hue sits where the [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) draws it. Dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward that colour.
195	
196	Red sits 103° counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock, just left of the top. Going counter-clockwise from there you'll find yellow on the left, green at the lower left, cyan near the bottom, blue on the right and magenta at the upper right. Every 75 % target on the vectorscope falls within about 12° of its place on the disc.
197	
198	## Reset the wheels
199	
200	| To reset | Do this |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| One wheel's push | Double-click its disc. The puck returns to the centre and the wheel's brightness stays. |
203	| One wheel's brightness | Double-click its strip. The value returns to 0 and the push stays. |
204	| All three wheels | Choose **Reset** in the section's header, or right-click the wheels and choose **Reset to default**. **Reset** appears once a wheel has moved, while no action is selected. |
205	
206	Each of these is one undo step, even when the first click of a double-click on the strip moved the knob. A double-click is named after its wheel, and resetting all three shows as **Undo Wheels**.
207	
208	## Grade several clips at once
209	
210	Select the clips and use the wheels as usual. Each control changes only its own values. A puck gives every selected clip that wheel's push and leaves each clip's brightness and other wheels alone. A strip or a field does the same for that wheel's brightness.
211	
212	The controls show the first clip's values. When the clips differ on any wheel, a **mixed** badge appears. One badge covers all three wheels.
213	
214	## Animate the wheels
215	
216	With an action selected, a puck, a strip or a field sets the action's end value, and the wheels ramp there from their values at the action's start. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
217	
218	While the action animates the wheels, a disc shows a hollow square at the start value and the puck in the action colour. A strip fills in the action colour from the start value. A coral mark shows the value under the playhead when it differs.
219	
220	The three wheels count as one row of the action. Moving any of them puts one [◆ in the gutter](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) beside all three, and removing the row takes all three out of the action. Right-click them for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**, or choose **Clear** in the section's header.
221	
222	## Good to know
223	
224	There's no Offset wheel. For an overall lift, use **Brightness** in the [Color section](/color/color-section/).
225	
226	## With an agent
227	
228	An agent can set the wheels with `set_video` as exact numbers, and an agent is the only way to enter a push by number. Each wheel takes a push as `x` and `y` and a brightness as `master`, all from −1 to 1. Its angles count the way the tooltip does, with red at 0° along positive `x`, and aren't turned to match the disc.
229	
230	Any wheel or value it leaves out stays as it is. Frame Job won't take a push past the rim from `set_video`, and says so rather than moving it to the rim. An action's end set with `set_action_end` is different: the value is kept, and the push stops at the rim while the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#wheels).
231
