240	title: Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves
241	description: Turn one colour toward another, or saturate or mute it, without touching the rest of the picture.
242	---
243	
244	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
245	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
246	
247	The hue curves work on one colour at a time. **Hue** turns a chosen hue toward another, such as making the greens more teal. **Sat** saturates or mutes a chosen hue, such as calming a loud red. Both leave the other colours alone.
248	
249	<AtAGlance
250	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ the Hue and Sat cells"
251	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
252	/>
253	
254	## The two hue channels
255	
256	The **Hue** and **Sat** cells in the channel picker put the plot into degrees. Each channel lays the colours out across the plot, and its height says what happens to the colour at that position.
257	
258	| Cell | Curve | Across | Up | The centre line |
259	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
260	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue | Hue, 0° to 360° | A shift, −180° to +180° | 0°, no shift |
261	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat | Hue, 0° to 360° | A gain, 0× to 2× | 1×, unchanged |
262	
263	So a straight hue channel is a flat line across the middle, not a diagonal. It starts with two points on that line, at 0° and 180°.
264	
265	Points work as they do on any curve: click to add one, drag, nudge, type, delete and reset. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/#edit-points). A channel holds 2 to 16 points.
266	
267	The hue curves run after **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** and before the [look](/color/looks/), so they read each colour as those curves left it. Both hue curves read that colour once, before either changes it. A **Sat** point on the greens still acts on greens you've turned teal with **Hue**.
268	
269	## The spectrum strip
270	
271	A strip under the plot shows which colour each position stands for, from 0° at the left to 360° at the right. Thin lines mark every 60°, with lines across at the quarters and a stronger line at the centre.
272	
273	| Hue | Colour |
274	| --- | --- |
275	| 0° | Red |
276	| 60° | Yellow |
277	| 120° | Green |
278	| 180° | Cyan |
279	| 240° | Blue |
280	| 300° | Magenta |
281	
282	## Hue vs Hue
283	
284	A positive shift moves a colour to the right along the strip, from red toward yellow and green. A negative shift moves it to the left. Brightness stays as it was.
285	
286	To make the greens more teal:
287	
288	<Steps>
289	
290	1. Select the clip, open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open **Curves** and click the **Hue** cell.
291	
292	2. Click the plot at about 90° and again at about 150°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
293	
294	3. Press the centre line at about 120° and drag up. The label beside the pointer shows the shift, such as `Hue 120° → +30°`.
295	
296	</Steps>
297	
298	The outer points are saved with the first point you move. Without them, the shift spreads as far as the points at 0° and 180°.
299	
300	## Hue vs Sat
301	
302	Above the centre line a hue gets more saturated, and below it less. At the bottom of the plot, 0×, that hue goes grey. At the top, 2×, its saturation doubles. Saturation scales around the colour's own brightness.
303	
304	To mute the reds:
305	
306	<Steps>
307	
308	1. With **Curves** open on the clip, click the **Sat** cell.
309	
310	2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
311	
312	3. Drag the point at 0°, at the left end of the centre line, down. The label beside the pointer shows the gain, such as `Hue 0° → ×0.60`.
313	
314	</Steps>
315	
316	## Hue curve safeguards
317	
318	- **A grey stays grey.** A grey has no real hue to read, so a hue curve never tints it. When a colour's strongest and weakest channels are within 2% of each other it's left alone, and the effect fades in to full strength at 6%.
319	- **Points never cross the wrap.** A point stops at 0° and 359.9°, so it can't slide round to the other end. The curve itself does wrap: its right end runs on smoothly into its left end, so a shift around red covers both ends of the plot.
320	- **Colours stay in range.** When a turned colour can't keep its brightness, it gives up some saturation rather than clip.
321	
322	## Good to know
323	
324	- The closest a point gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.1°.
325	- **Reset Hue** and **Reset Sat** straighten one channel from the cell's right-click menu. The section's **Reset** straightens all six, the tone curves included. See [Reset curves](/color/curves/#reset-curves).
326	- The **Hue** slider in the [Color section](/color/color-section/) turns every colour at once. Hue vs Hue turns only the colours you choose.
327	- Hue curves animate inside an action as tone curves do. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
328	
329	## With an agent
330	
331	An agent writes `hue_hue` and `hue_sat` whole, each as a list of 2 to 16 hue and value pairs, and that list replaces the channel. It can place a point anywhere from 0 up to, but not including, 360. A value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#curves).
332

346	
347	Curves change the picture's tones with points on a line. Use **Master** for contrast and the black and white points, and **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** to work on one colour at a time. The picture goes through the curves after the [wheels](/color/wheels/) and before the [look](/color/looks/).
348	
349	<AtAGlance
350	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', 'Esc', '← → ↑ ↓']}
351	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Curves', 'Right-click a channel cell for Reset']}
352	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
353	/>
354	
355	<Shot
356	  name="05g-clip-curves.inspector"
357	  alt="The Curves section open on the Color tab. Six cells read Master, Red, Green, Blue, Hue and Sat, with Master chosen and a dot under Master and Red. Below them a square plot shows a gentle S-curve in black through four points, with the changed Red curve as a faint line behind it. Under the plot are empty In and Out fields and a greyed Delete button."
358	/>
359	
360	## The Curves section
361	
362	Select a video, image or still clip, or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) and open **Curves**. The section starts closed, and its header reads "neutral" until a curve changes, then "adjusted".
363	
364	The section has three parts, from top to bottom:
365	
366	- The channel picker, which chooses the curve you're editing.
367	- The plot, a square with a 4 × 4 grid. It grows with the inspector up to 300 pt wide.
368	- The selected point's **In** and **Out** fields, and **Delete**.
369	
370	Across the plot is the level going in, from 0 at the left to 1 at the right. Up the plot is the level coming out. A thin diagonal marks a straight curve, which changes nothing.
371	
372	## The channel picker
373	
374	Six cells above the plot choose the channel you edit. Click a different cell, and any selected point is deselected.
375	
376	| Cell | What it changes |
377	| --- | --- |
378	| **Master** | All three colours together. Use it for contrast and for the black and white points. |
379	| **Red** | The red channel only. |
380	| **Green** | The green channel only. |
381	| **Blue** | The blue channel only. |
382	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue, which turns a chosen hue toward another. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
383	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat, which saturates or mutes a chosen hue. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
384	
385	**Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** are the tone curves, and **Hue** and **Sat** are the hue curves.
386	
387	There's no separate luma curve. **Master** runs first, then each colour goes through its own channel, so a **Red** curve works on what **Master** has already done.
388	
389	---
390	title: Filters
391	description: Stack up to four filters on a clip, from Blur and Pixelate to Sepia and Vignette, set how strong each one is, and animate them.
392	---
393	
394	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
395	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
396	
397	Filters change how a clip looks: soften it, break it into blocks, turn it black and white, darken its corners. A clip can carry up to four at once, and any clip that draws can have them, text, shapes and graphics included.
398	
399	<AtAGlance
400	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Filters"
401	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'paste_attributes']}
402	/>
403	
404	## Add a filter
405	
406	<Steps>
407	
408	1. Select the clip and open the **Clip** tab's [**Picture**](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab.
409	
410	2. Open the **Filters** section. On a clip with none it reads "No filters on this clip."
411	
412	3. Choose **Add Filter**. A Blur at 50 % joins the end of the stack.
413	
414	4. Pick the filter you want in the row's popup that reads **Blur**, and set its **Amount**.
415	
416	</Steps>
417	
418	Changing a filter's kind keeps its **Amount**. A clip can hold four, as the "4 at most" beside **Add Filter** says, and the button greys out at that point.
419	
420	Each change is one undo step. While the section is closed, its header shows `none`, the filter's name, or a count such as `3 filters`.
421	
422	## The seven filters
423	
424	| Filter | What it does | At 100 % |
425	| --- | --- | --- |
426	| **Blur** | Softens the picture. | A radius of 24 pixels |
427	| **Sharpen** | Crisps up edges and fine detail with an unsharp mask. | A gain of 2 |
428	| **Pixelate** | Breaks the picture into square blocks. The clip's edge and rounded corners stay clean. | Blocks 64 pixels across |
429	| **Sepia** | Gives the picture a warm old-photo tone. | The full tone |
430	| **Noir** | Turns the picture black and white and adds contrast. Taking **Saturation** to its lowest only removes the colour. | Fully black and white |
431	| **Vignette** | Darkens towards the edges in an ellipse fitted to the clip's cropped shape. The darkening starts a little under halfway from the centre to the corners. | Black corners |
432	| **Invert** | Turns the picture into its negative. | The full negative |
433	
434	Blur and Pixelate are measured in the clip's own pixels. Scale a clip up and the effect grows with it, and the same **Amount** looks finer on a 4K clip than on a 1080p one.
435	
436	## Set how strong a filter is
437	
438	**Amount** runs from 0 to 100 %, with quick picks at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. At 0 the filter stays on the clip and does nothing. Sepia, Noir and Invert mix from the original picture towards their full effect as the number rises.
439	
440	## Stack and reorder filters
441	
442	Each filter's row starts with a number popup, which is its place in the stack. Pick a different number to move the filter. You can't drag rows. A move is one undo step.
443	
444	The place doesn't decide everything, because Frame Job always works through a stack in this order:
445	
446	1. Pixelate, whatever its place.
447	2. The **Color** section of the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/): **Brightness**, **Contrast**, **Saturation** and **Hue**.
448	3. Blur and Sharpen, whatever their places.
449	4. The rest of the Color tab: **Light**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look**.
450	5. Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert, in the order of their places.
451	
452	So the order only changes the picture among Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert. Noir then Sepia gives a warm black and white, while Sepia then Noir gives a plain one. Moving a Blur above or below a Sepia changes nothing.
453	
454	Filters of the same kind combine:
455	
456	| In one stack | You get |
457	| --- | --- |
458	| Two Blurs | One wider blur. Two at 100 % reach a radius of about 34 pixels, and four reach 48. |
459	| Two Sharpens | The sum of the two. |
460	| Two Pixelates | The coarser of the two. |
461	
462	## Remove a filter
463	
464	Choose **Remove** in the filter's row. **Reset** in the section's header takes off the whole stack, and it's there only while no action is selected.
465	
466	## Animate a filter
467	
468	An [action](/motion/actions/) can ramp a filter's **Amount**, for example a blur that builds across a clip.
469	
470	<Steps>
471	
472	1. Add the filter and set **Amount** to where the ramp should start.
473	
474	2. Add an action on the clip and keep it selected.
475	
476	3. Set **Amount** to where the ramp should end.
477	
478	</Steps>
479	
480	With an action selected, each control does something different:
481	
482	| You change | What happens |
483	| --- | --- |
484	| **Amount** | It ramps across the action. |
485	| The filter's kind | It switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end". The other filters keep ramping. |
486	| The filter's place | It moves at the action's end. |
487	| **Add Filter** or **Remove** | It changes the clip itself rather than the action, so it isn't animated. |
488	
489	:::caution
490	Adding or removing a filter while an action already animates the stack leaves the two stacks different lengths. The action stops ramping them and the filters switch at its end instead. To get the ramp back, select the action, choose **Clear** in the section's header, then set the clip's amounts and the action's again.
491	:::
492	
493	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how the rows behave in an action.
494	
495	## Filters on an adjustment clip
496	
497	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no **Picture** sub-tab, so it can't take a filter from the inspector. It gets one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) instead.
498	
499	<Steps>
500	
501	1. Put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert on an ordinary clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
502	
503	2. Select the adjustment clip.
504	
505	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
506	
507	</Steps>
508	
509	The filter then applies to everything behind the adjustment clip for as long as it lasts, and to nothing on a track in front.
510	
511	Blur, Sharpen and Pixelate can't go on an adjustment clip, because it has no picture of its own to sample. Pasting from a clip that has one stops with an error naming the clip and the filter, and changes nothing.
512	
513	:::caution
514	Paste Attributes replaces the target's picture settings, not only its filters. Pasting onto an adjustment clip overwrites its grade and its Strength with the copied clip's, so paste first and grade afterwards.
515	:::
516	
517	## Good to know
518	
519	- A filter covers the whole picture for the whole clip. To blur or pixelate one region, such as a face, use [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
520	- With several clips selected, the rows show the first clip's stack, and any edit gives every selected clip that whole stack.
521	- A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the Filters section, but a filter on it has no effect. Put filters on the clips inside the nest.
522	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), a clip's filters shape the cut it makes. **Alpha** and **Inverted Alpha** read only transparency, so Sharpen, Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert change nothing there.
523	- A clip's [reflection](/effects/reflection/) shows its filters too.
524	
525	## With an agent
526	
527	An agent sets a clip's filters with `set_video`, as a list of kinds and amounts, with each amount from 0 to 1. The list replaces the old one whole, so it sends every filter it wants to keep, and an empty list clears the stack. A fifth filter is an error, and nothing changes. It can put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert straight onto an adjustment clip, with no paste. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#filters).
528	
529	With `set_action_end`, an agent can give an action a list of a different length, which switches at the action's end rather than ramping. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).
530	
531	## Related

title: "The Preview Window"
description: Show the picture in a second window with no handles or guides, on another display or full screen.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Preview Window shows the picture on its own, with no handles or guides over it. Use it to put the picture on a second display while you edit in the main window.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Window" keys="⇧⌘P" />

## Open the Preview Window

Press <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd> or choose **View ▸ Preview Window**. The same key hides it again, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's open. It opens on an empty timeline too, where the window is black.

The window is titled after the project, for example "Intro — Preview", and has a black surround. You can resize it down to 320 × 200, and it can go full screen.

It uses the same player as the main preview, so the two never drift apart. [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection** and **Show SDR Version** all apply to it, but the [corner tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags) don't appear in it.

The window is only for looking. Safe-area guides, zoom and the handles for moving clips stay in the main preview.

## Remembered position

The window remembers its position and size between launches, so it opens where you last left it, on a second display for example. The first time, it opens at 640 × 360 in the middle of the screen. It stays visible when you switch to another app.

It closes with its project window. Whether it's open isn't remembered, so it starts off in each new window.

## Keys

The window doesn't take you away from the editor. While it has the focus:

- Playback keys work: <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd>, <kbd>L</kbd>, the arrows, Home and End.
- The editor's other single-letter keys work too, such as <kbd>M</kbd> for a marker or <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> for the range.
- Every editor ⌘ command works, so <kbd>⌘E</kbd> opens the export sheet and <kbd>⌘T</kbd> splits.
- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> undoes the project's last step, and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> redoes it, the same steps as in the editor.
- <kbd>⌘W</kbd> closes the Preview Window, not the project.

Single-letter keys stop while a field in the editor window is being edited, or while the editor has a sheet open.

## Good to know

- There's one saved position for every project. With two projects' Preview Windows open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved to.
- The window isn't listed in the **Window** menu. Use **View ▸ Preview Window** to find it.
- After you save a project under a new name, the title updates the next time you show the window.

## Related

- [The preview](/timeline/preview/)
- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
- [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/)

title: "Canvas background and timecode"
description: "Set the colour behind every layer, make the canvas transparent, choose how times are shown, and decide how new clips are sized."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) sets three things for the whole project: the colour behind your clips, how times are written, and how big a new clip starts.

<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Appearance" tools={['set_canvas', 'add_clip']} />

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background** | The colour behind every layer. | Black, opaque |
| **Timecode** | How the project shows a time. | Frames |
| **Fit new clips to canvas** | Scales down a new clip that's bigger than the canvas. | On |

A change to **Timecode** or **Fit new clips to canvas** is one undo step.

## Set the background colour

Click the **Background** swatch and pick a colour in the Colors panel. The colour sits behind every layer, so it shows wherever no clip covers the canvas.

To put a colour on the timeline as a clip instead, see [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).

## Make the background transparent

Lower the opacity in the Colors panel. The swatch shows a checkerboard behind the colour, and the **Background** row of the [Document summary](/projects/document-tab/#the-document-summary) reads `Transparent`, or the colour with its opacity.

Most export formats can't carry transparency, so while the background isn't fully opaque, the section adds a note about the formats that can.

| The note says | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." | Three or more formats keep it, so the note counts them. They're HEVC with Alpha (MOV), VP9 with Alpha (WebM), ProRes 4444 (MOV) and Animated PNG. |
| "Transparent — needs an alpha format." | Frame Job can't name the formats yet, which can happen on a project with nothing on the timeline. |

See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).

## Choose a timecode format

**Timecode** sets how times are written everywhere the project shows one, including the toolbar, the ruler, the inspector, markers and the transcript.

| Choice | Looks like |
| --- | --- |
| **Frames** | `HH:MM:SS:FF` |
| **Milliseconds** | `HH:MM:SS.mmm` |

**Frames** doesn't drop frames, so at 29.97 fps the count runs slightly behind the clock over a long timeline.

## Fit new clips to canvas

This decides how big a new clip starts. It's on by default.

| Setting | A clip bigger than the canvas | Any other clip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On | Starts at Fit scale: scaled down until all of it shows. | Starts at 100 %, its native size. |
| Off | Starts at 100 %, so it runs past the edges of the canvas. | Starts at 100 %. |

A clip counts as bigger when either its width or its height is larger than the canvas. Fit never scales a clip up, and changing the setting leaves clips already on the timeline as they are. To fit or fill one clip, see [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/).

## Reset the section

**Reset** on the **Appearance** header puts all three back to their defaults: opaque black, **Frames** and on. It's offered only while one of them differs, and it's one undo step.

## With an agent

[`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas) sets all three, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value.

| Argument | What it takes |
| --- | --- |
| `background` | Four numbers from 0 to 1, `[r, g, b, a]`. Three numbers, or one outside the range, fails and nothing changes. |
| `timecode_frames` | `true` for **Frames**, `false` for **Milliseconds**. |
| `fit_new_clips` | `true` or `false`, as the checkbox. |

[`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_clip) follows **Fit new clips to canvas** as the app does. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).

## Related

- [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/)
- [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/)
- [Image clips](/text-and-shapes/image-clips/)
- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

title: "Burn in timecode"
description: Draw the project's timecode into an exported picture, so a reviewer's notes point at exact frames.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Burn in timecode draws the project's timecode into the exported picture. Use it for a review copy, so a note about a frame carries the number you'll find on your timeline.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Burn in timecode"
  tools={['export', 'render_frame']}
/>

## Burn in timecode

Choose **File ▸ Export…** and turn on **Burn in timecode**. It's off by default.

The timecode appears only in the exported file, never in the preview. It sits centred near the bottom of the picture, on a translucent black plate, on top of everything, captions included.

The box works on every format with a picture, Animated GIF and Animated PNG included. It's greyed out for the audio-only formats, and **File ▸ Save Frame…** never offers it.

The sheet remembers it with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## What the timecode shows

It uses the project's own timecode format, as the toolbar shows it: `HH:MM:SS:FF` or `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, non-drop. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

It shows **project time**. A file exported from an [in/out range](/export/range/) that starts at 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 in a player, but its first frame reads 00:00:10:00. That's the number a reviewer's note needs.

## With an agent

`burn_in_timecode` turns it on in `export`, and it's off by default. `render_frame` takes the same argument, so an agent can draw the timecode into a single frame, which **Save Frame…** can't do. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)

title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
/>

## Repackage or convert a file

<Steps>

1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."

2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.

3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.

</Steps>

The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:

| The button | What the alert tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |

If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.

A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.

## What's copied and what's re-encoded

Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.

| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
| Sound | AAC, ALAC and the usual 16-, 24- and 32-bit PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |

The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.

VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. Frame Job then checks that every frame of the copy sits exactly on the frame rate. If the copy fails that check, or won't open, it's re-encoded to H.264 once. Unless you've told Frame Job to do this automatically, it asks you again first.

Only the first video stream and the first audio stream are carried over. Subtitles and data streams are dropped.

fixed.question: Is the viewer colour managed? Why does my export look different?

fixed.change: timeline/preview-window: honest note that it is an ordinary window and there is no such output.

fixed.change: reference/file-formats: new section 'Timelines from other editors'. export/prores says a rendered master is how a finished timeline leaves Frame Job.

fixed.question: Shot match, auto balance, white balance picker?
fixed.change: color/light says none exists and points to balancing on the Parade.

fixed.question: Video noise reduction, film grain, OFX plugins?
fixed.change: effects/filters: honest note, plus a link for readers who wanted audio noise reduction.

fixed.question: ProRes 422 HQ, LT, Proxy, 4444 XQ?
fixed.change: export/prores says only standard 422 and 4444 are written. Code gives AVVideoCodecType.proRes422, and ffprobe read the Standard profile from a test file.

fixed.question: Trim pass, tone mapping, two deliverables; HDR10+?
fixed.change: hdr/show-sdr-version names the fixed tone map, with no settings and no trim, and says one grade drives both pictures. hdr/export-hdr says no HDR10+ and that a master and its SDR version are two exports.

fixed.question: Rec. 709 gamma 2.4 or 2.2; full or legal range?
fixed.change: export/what-an-export-includes says exports are video range with no full-range option, and there is no display gamma choice. Measured: white Y 234, black 16, flagged tv, for H.264 and ProRes 422 written by a scratch AVAssetWriter test using the app's half-float frame format and BT.709 tags, not by a real Frame Job export. AV1 and VP9 are stated in the code.

fixed.question: Smart render, pass-through, generation loss?
fixed.change: export/what-an-export-includes says every frame is drawn and encoded again.

fixed.question: Why does it look washed out, clipped, too contrasty, or lose its grade?
fixed.change: reference/troubleshooting: new section 'The picture looks wrong', a table that goes from symptom to cause and fix.

fixed.question: Broadcast safe, gamut warning, false colour?
fixed.change: color/waveform-and-parade says clip marks and readouts are the only warning, and that 0 to 100 % exports as legal levels.

fixed.question: Why does 4K log stutter? Proxies, optimised media, render cache?
fixed.change: timeline/preview-quality says none exist, and what to do when decoding is the bottleneck.

fixed.question: What happens to my grade on split, speed change or relink?
fixed.change: color/color-tab, editing/splitting and projects/relink-media all state that the grade stays with the clip.

fixed.question: PQ timeline; nits; 32-bit float; LUT interpolation; source timecode
fixed.change: Short facts added. hdr/dynamic-range: no PQ working space. hdr/hdr-scopes, hdr/how-sources-are-read and reference/glossary: nits. hdr/precision: no 32-bit float mode. color/luts: trilinear interpolation. projects/background-and-timecode: count starts at zero, no source timecode, no timecode track.

unanswerable: How an HDR (HLG) project's preview looks on a given display: the code hands the picture to an AVPlayerLayer and macOS decides from there. The page only says it depends on the display, and to trust the scopes.

Whether ProRes RAW imports: nothing in the code mentions it, and the first-frame decode check would decide on each Mac, so it is left out. Blackmagic RAW, R3D and ARRIRAW are stated as not importing because nothing in the code registers a decoder for them.
Whether V-Log L can use the V-Log row: the code has only the V-Log curve and says nothing about V-Log L, so I added no claim.

fixed.question: Are there nodes? Serial, parallel or layer grades? What is the order of operations?
fixed.change: color/color-tab: the fixed grade order now uses the words pipeline and order of operations, says there are no nodes or layer mixer, and says stacked adjustment clips are the way to grade on top of a grade.

fixed.question: Which logs are supported, and what about LogC, Log3G10, S-Log2, N-Log, F-Log, D-Log? What is the input transform?
fixed.change: hdr/camera-log says it is the input transform and names the logs with no built-in curve, sending them to a maker's LUT. hdr/log-luts carries the same words in its opening. hdr/how-sources-are-read calls itself the colour management and adds that there is no ACES mode or other working space.

fixed.question: Is the viewer colour managed? Why does my export look different?
fixed.change: timeline/preview: new section 'Colour on your display' (macOS draws the picture, no viewer LUT or calibration setting, trust the scopes). export/what-an-export-includes#colour-labels is now a table of primaries, transfer and matrix with 1-1-1, 9-18-9 and 9-16-9, and it explains why a file can look lighter or darker elsewhere.

fixed.question: Can I feed a reference monitor (SDI, I/O card, clean feed)?
fixed.change: timeline/preview-window: honest note that it is an ordinary window and there is no such output.

fixed.question: Can I save a grade or look, keep versions or stills, or export a LUT?
fixed.change: color/copy-a-grade: new section 'Keep a grade for later' (none of these exist; Paste Attributes works across projects, so a project of graded clips can act as a library). color/looks cross-links to it.

fixed.question: Split wipe, or bypassing one clip's grade?
fixed.change: color/show-ungraded: says it bypasses every grade at once, and that there is no wipe and no per-clip bypass.

fixed.question: Adjustment layer, timeline grade, keyframing a grade (the reader's words)
fixed.change: color/adjustment-clips and color/animate-a-grade now carry 'adjustment layer', 'timeline grade' and 'keyframe'. Both questions were already answered; this was for search only.

fixed.question: Secondaries, HSL key, power windows, tracked masks?
fixed.change: color/qualifiers names secondary correction and HSL key. color/adjustment-clips says a matte is the power window or mask, moved by hand with an action; a shape has no feather, so a soft edge needs a soft-edged picture; nothing tracks.

fixed.question: Luma vs Sat, Hue vs Luma, Sat vs Sat curves?
fixed.change: color/hue-curves says these do not exist.
